He said: "Hud has made me grey, and al-Waqi'ah, and 'Amma yatasa'alun, and 'Idha al-shamsu kuwwirat." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/102). It is munqati' (disconnected in its chain), and al-Hafiz al-Daraqutni discussed it and the following one at sufficient length in al-'Ilal (3/193–211).]]

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Shayban, from Abu Ishaq, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have grown grey?" He said: "Hud has made me grey, and al-Waqi'ah, and al-Mursalat, and 'Amma yatasa'alun, and 'Idha al-shamsu kuwwirat." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3297). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith, which we only know from Ibn 'Abbas through this route."]] And in another narration: "Hud and its sisters."

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abdan ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Hammad [[All copies say "Hajjaj," and the correction is from al-Mu'jam al-Kabir.]] ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Salam narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hud and its sisters have made me grey: al-Waqi'ah, al-Haqqah, and 'Idha al-shamsu kuwwirat." And in another narration: "Hud and its sisters." [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/183). al-Daraqutni narrated it in al-'Ilal (1/210) by way of Ahmad ibn Tariq with the same chain. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (3/192): "'Umar ibn Sahban is matruk (abandoned)," and Sa'id ibn Salam is a liar.]]

It has also been narrated from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Tariq al-Ra'ishi [[In T and A, and in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: "al-Wabshi," and I have not found his biography.]] narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what has made you grey?" He said: "Hud and al-Waqi'ah." [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/125, 126). In it, the chain is through 'Amr ibn Thabit from Abu Ishaq from Abu al-Ahwas from Ibn Mas'ud, so perhaps it fell out of Ibn Kathir's copy, and Allah knows best. For further hadiths on this topic, the scholar Muhammad Tarhuni has extensively traced them; see his book Mawsu'at Fada'il al-Qur'an (1/295–308).]]

'Amr ibn Thabit is matruk, and Abu Ishaq did not meet Ibn Mas'ud. And Allah knows best.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The discussion of the disjointed letters (huruf al-hija') has already been given at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated here. And success is from Allah.

As for His saying: ﴿Its verses have been made firm, then detailed﴾, meaning: they are firm (muhkamah) in their wording and detailed (mufassalah) in their meaning, so it is complete in form and meaning. This is the meaning reported from Mujahid and Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

* *

His saying: ﴿from One who is Wise and Acquainted﴾ means: from Allah, the Wise in His sayings and His rulings, the Acquainted with the ends of matters.

﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾ means: this Qur'an, firm and detailed, was sent down so that Allah alone, without partner, be worshipped, as He said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25], and He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl: 36].

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾ [[In T and A: "Inni".]] means: I am a warner to you of the punishment if you oppose Him, and a bringer of good tidings of reward if you obey Him, as in the authentic hadith: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ climbed al-Safa and called the clans of Quraysh, the nearest and then the nearest, and they gathered. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, what do you think, if I told you that cavalry were about to attack you in the morning, would you believe me?" They said: "We have never found you to lie." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." [[Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (4971), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And that you seek forgiveness of your Lord, then repent to Him; He will give you enjoyment, a good enjoyment, until a specified term, and will give every person of merit his merit﴾ means: and I command you to seek forgiveness for past sins and to repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for what you will face in the future, and that you persist in that. ﴿He will give you enjoyment, a good enjoyment﴾ means: in this world. ﴿Until a specified term﴾ ﴿and will give every person of merit his merit﴾ means: in the Hereafter. This is said by Qatadah, like His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97]. [[In T: "fa-la-yuhyiyannahu."]] [[In T: "bi-ahsan alladhi kanu."]] And it has come in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Sa'd: "Indeed, you will not spend an expenditure seeking the Face of Allah except that you will be rewarded for it, even what you put into the mouth of your wife." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (6373) and Sahih Muslim (1628).]] [[In T and A: "in fam".]]

Ibn Jarir said: I was told, from al-Musayyab ibn Sharik, from Abu Bakr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿and will give every person of merit his merit﴾, that he said: Whoever does an evil deed, an evil deed is written against him; and whoever does a good deed, ten good deeds are written for him. If he is punished in this world for the evil deed he did, the ten good deeds remain for him; and if he is not punished for it in this world, one of the ten good deeds is taken and nine good deeds remain for him. Then he said: "Destroyed is the one whose units overcome his tens." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/231).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾ is a severe threat to whoever turns away from the commands of Allah, the Exalted, and denies His messengers, for the punishment will surely reach him on the Day of his return. ﴿To Allah is your return﴾ means: your return on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And He is Competent over all things﴾ means: He is capable of whatever He wills, of bestowing His favour upon His friends, avenging Himself upon His enemies, and restoring all creation on the Day of Resurrection. This is the station of warning, just as the former was the station of encouragement.

As for His saying: ﴿Its verses have been made firm, then detailed﴾, meaning: they are firm (muhkamah) in their wording and detailed (mufassalah) in their meaning, so it is complete in form and meaning. This is the meaning reported from Mujahid and Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

* *

His saying: ﴿from One who is Wise and Acquainted﴾ means: from Allah, the Wise in His sayings and His rulings, the Acquainted with the ends of matters.

﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾ means: this Qur'an, firm and detailed, was sent down so that Allah alone, without partner, be worshipped, as He said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25], and He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl: 36].

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾ [[In T and A: "Inni".]] means: I am a warner to you of the punishment if you oppose Him, and a bringer of good tidings of reward if you obey Him, as in the authentic hadith: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ climbed al-Safa and called the clans of Quraysh, the nearest and then the nearest, and they gathered. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, what do you think, if I told you that cavalry were about to attack you in the morning, would you believe me?" They said: "We have never found you to lie." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." [[Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (4971), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And that you seek forgiveness of your Lord, then repent to Him; He will give you enjoyment, a good enjoyment, until a specified term, and will give every person of merit his merit﴾ means: and I command you to seek forgiveness for past sins and to repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for what you will face in the future, and that you persist in that. ﴿He will give you enjoyment, a good enjoyment﴾ means: in this world. ﴿Until a specified term﴾ ﴿and will give every person of merit his merit﴾ means: in the Hereafter. This is said by Qatadah, like His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97]. [[In T: "fa-la-yuhyiyannahu."]] [[In T: "bi-ahsan alladhi kanu."]] And it has come in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Sa'd: "Indeed, you will not spend an expenditure seeking the Face of Allah except that you will be rewarded for it, even what you put into the mouth of your wife." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (6373) and Sahih Muslim (1628).]] [[In T and A: "in fam".]]

Ibn Jarir said: I was told, from al-Musayyab ibn Sharik, from Abu Bakr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿and will give every person of merit his merit﴾, that he said: Whoever does an evil deed, an evil deed is written against him; and whoever does a good deed, ten good deeds are written for him. If he is punished in this world for the evil deed he did, the ten good deeds remain for him; and if he is not punished for it in this world, one of the ten good deeds is taken and nine good deeds remain for him. Then he said: "Destroyed is the one whose units overcome his tens." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/231).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾ is a severe threat to whoever turns away from the commands of Allah, the Exalted, and denies His messengers, for the punishment will surely reach him on the Day of his return. ﴿To Allah is your return﴾ means: your return on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And He is Competent over all things﴾ means: He is capable of whatever He wills, of bestowing His favour upon His friends, avenging Himself upon His enemies, and restoring all creation on the Day of Resurrection. This is the station of warning, just as the former was the station of encouragement.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They used to dislike facing the sky with their private parts (furuj) and while relieving themselves (haal waqqa'ihim), so Allah revealed this verse." It was narrated by al-Bukhari from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far, that Ibn 'Abbas recited: "Surely they fold their breasts (innahum tathnuni sudurahum)," and I said: "O Abu 'Abbas, what is 'tathnuni sudurahum'?" He said: "A man would have intercourse with his wife and feel shy, or would relieve himself and feel shy, so this was revealed: 'Surely they fold their breasts.'"

In another wording from him: Ibn 'Abbas said: "There were people who were shy to relieve themselves, so that they would expose themselves to the sky, and to have intercourse with their wives, so that they would expose themselves to the sky. So this was revealed concerning them."

Then he said: al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, 'Amr narrated to us, who said: Ibn 'Abbas recited: "Surely they fold their breasts so that they may hide from Him. Certainly, when they cover themselves with their garments" (alla hina yastaghshuna thiyabahum).

Al-Bukhari said: Others besides him said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "yastaghshuna" (they cover themselves) means they cover their heads.

Ibn 'Abbas also said in another narration, explaining this verse: "It means doubt about Allah and the doing of evil deeds." Similarly it was narrated from Mujahid, al-Hasan and others: that is, they used to fold their breasts when they said or did something, thinking that by this they were hiding from Allah. So Allah the Exalted informed them that He knows them when they cover themselves with their garments during their sleep in the darkness of the night, "He knows what they conceal" of speech, "and what they reveal." "Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts" — that is, He knows what their breasts harbour of intentions, inner thoughts and secrets.

How excellent is what Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said in his well-known Mu'allaqa:

"So do not hide from Allah what is in your souls, that it may be concealed; for whatever you conceal, Allah knows it.

It is deferred and recorded in a book, and stored up for a Day of Reckoning; or it is hastened and then requited."

This pre-Islamic poet acknowledged the existence of the Creator, His knowledge of particulars, the Return, the recompense, and the recording of deeds in scrolls for the Day of Resurrection.

'Abdullah ibn Shaddad said: "Whenever one of them passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would fold his breast and cover his head, so Allah revealed this."

The return of the pronoun to Allah is preferable, because of His saying: "Certainly, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal."

Ibn 'Abbas also recited "Surely they fold their breasts (yathnuni sudurahum)" with the word "sudur" in the nominative as the subject (fa'iliyyah), and its meaning is close.

Allah, the Exalted, informs that He is responsible for the provision of all creatures, of every beast of the earth, small and large, those of the sea and those of the land. And that He ﴿knows where they settle and where they are lodged﴾. That is, He knows where their journey on the earth ends, and where each one returns to its nest. The ﴿mustawda'ahā﴾ (where it is lodged) is its resting place.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah and others related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿wa-yaʿlamu mustaqarrahā﴾ (and He knows its settling place) means where it shelters, and ﴿wa-mustawdaʿahā﴾ (and its lodging place) means where it dies.

From Mujāhid: ﴿mustaqarrahā﴾ means in the womb, and ﴿mustawdaʿahā﴾ means in the loins, like the wording in Sūrat al-Anʿām. It was similarly related from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and a group of others. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned the statements of the exegetes here, as he mentioned them at that verse: [[At the explanation of verse 98 of Sūrat al-Anʿām.]] So Allah knows best. All of that is written in a clear Book with Allah, which encompasses all of it, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ [al-Anʿām: 38]. And His statement [[In A and T: "And Allah, the Exalted, said."]]: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows what is on the land and the sea. And not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear Book﴾ [al-Anʿām: 59].

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 11, verses 7–8:

He, may He be exalted, informs of His power over all things, and that He created the heavens and the earth in six days, and that His Throne was upon the water before that, as Imam Ahmad said:

Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Jami' ibn Shaddad, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Accept the glad tidings, O Banu Tamim." They said: "You have given us glad tidings, so give us [something]." He said: "Accept the glad tidings, O people of Yemen." They said: "We have accepted, so inform us about the beginning of this matter, how was it?" He said: "Allah was before everything, and His Throne was upon the water, and He wrote in the Preserved Tablet the mention of everything." He said: "Then someone came to me and said: 'O Imran, your she-camel has broken loose from her tether.' So I went out following her, and I do not know what happened after me."[[Musnad (4/431).]]

This hadith is recorded in the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim with many wordings.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (3190, 3191, 4365, 4386, 7418). I did not find it in Sahih Muslim.]] Among them: They said: "We have come to you asking about the beginning of this matter," and he said: "Allah was, and there was nothing before Him" (and in another narration: "other than Him"; and in another: "with Him"), "and His Throne was upon the water, and He wrote in the Reminder (al-Dhikr) everything. Then He created the heavens and the earth."

In Sahih Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah decreed the measures of the creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was upon the water."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2653).]]

Al-Bukhari said in the tafsir of this verse: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Spend, and I will spend upon you.'" And he said: "The Hand of Allah is full; it is not diminished by expenditure, pouring night and day." And he said: "Have you considered what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? For it has not diminished what is in His Hand, and His Throne was upon the water, and in His Hand is the Scale, lowering and raising."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4684).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama informed us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata, from Wakee' ibn Udus, from his paternal uncle Abu Razin, whose name is Luqayt ibn Amir ibn al-Muntafiq al-Uqayli, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, where was our Lord before He created His creation?" He said: "He was in a cloud ('ama'), with nothing beneath it and nothing above it. Then He created the Throne after that."

This was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir and Ibn Majah in the Sunan, through the hadith of Yazid ibn Harun. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan (good) hadith."[[Musnad (4/11); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3109); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (182).]]

Mujahid said regarding ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾: before He created anything. Likewise said Wahb ibn Munabbih, Damra ibn Habib, and Qatada, and Ibn Jarir, and others.

Qatada said regarding His words ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾: "It informs you how the beginning of His creation was before He created the heavens and the earth."

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said regarding ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾: "When He created the heavens and the earth, He divided that water into two halves, and made half beneath the Throne, and it is the Sealed Sea (al-Bahr al-Masjur)."

Ibn Abbas said: "The Throne was only named 'Throne' because of its height."

Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid said: I heard Sa'd al-Ta'i say: "The Throne is a red ruby."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water﴾: "So it was as He described Himself, for there was nothing but the water, and upon it the Throne, and upon the Throne the Lord of Majesty and Honour, Might and Authority, Dominion and Power, Forbearance and Knowledge, Mercy and Blessing, the Doer of what He wills."

Al-A'mash narrated from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about the words of Allah: ﴿And His Throne was upon the water﴾: "Upon what was the water?" He said: "Upon the back of the wind."

* *

As for His words, ﴿that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾: that is, He created the heavens and the earth for the benefit of His servants, whom He created so that they would worship Him alone, with no partner, and He did not create that in vain, as He said: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad: 27]. And He said: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us? Exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115–116]. And He said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56].

* *

As for His words, ﴿that He may test you﴾: that is, to try you, ﴿as to which of you is best in deed﴾. He did not say "most in deed," but ﴿best in deed﴾. An action is not good unless it is sincerely for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and in accordance with the Sharia (law) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whenever an action lacks one of these two conditions, it is invalid and nullified.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And if you say, "Indeed, you will be resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is nothing but obvious magic."﴾ The Exalted says: And if you inform these polytheists, O Muhammad, that Allah will resurrect them after their death as He originated them, while they know that Allah, the Exalted, is the One who created the heavens and the earth, [as He said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87], ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [al-Ankabut: 61]], and yet they deny the resurrection and the return on the Day of Judgment, which is, in relation to power, easier than the origination, as He said: ﴿And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27], and He said: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28]. Their words ﴿This is nothing but obvious magic﴾ mean: they say, out of disbelief and obstinacy, "We do not confirm to you the occurrence of the resurrection, and no one who mentions that is following you except someone you have bewitched, so he follows you in what you say."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a limited community, they will surely say, "What is holding it back?"﴾ The Exalted says: If We delay the punishment and the retribution from these polytheists until a known term and a restricted limit, and We threaten them with it until an appointed period, they will surely say, out of denial and haste, ﴿"What is holding it back?"﴾, that is, "What is delaying this punishment from us?" Their natures have become accustomed to denial and doubt, so there is no escape or refuge for them from it.

The word "ummah" is used in the Qur'an and the Sunnah with several meanings. It is used to mean a period of time, as in His words in this verse: ﴿until a limited community﴾, and His words in [Surah] Yusuf: ﴿And the one of the two who was saved said, after a period (ummah), and he remembered﴾ [Yusuf: 45]. It is used for an imam who is followed, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a ummah, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [al-Nahl: 120]. It is used for religion and creed, as in His words, reporting about the polytheists that they said: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a ummah, and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23]. It is used for a group, as in His words: ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found upon it a group (ummah) of people watering﴾ [al-Qasas: 23], and He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every ummah a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl: 36], and He said: ﴿And for every ummah is a messenger, and when their messenger comes, judgment will be made between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Yunus: 47].

The meaning of "ummah" here is: those among whom the Messenger is sent, both their believers and their disbelievers, as in Sahih Muslim: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, no one from this ummah hears of me, a Jew or a Christian, and then dies without believing in me, except that he will enter the Fire."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (153), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

As for the ummah of the followers, they are those who believe in the messengers, as He said: ﴿You are the best ummah brought forth for mankind﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110]. And in the Sahih: "Then I will say: My ummah, my ummah."

The word ummah is also used for a faction and a group, as in His words: ﴿And among the people of Moses is an ummah who guide by truth and by it act justly﴾ [al-A'raf: 159], and He said: ﴿Among the People of the Scripture is an upright ummah who recite the verses of Allah during the night, and they prostrate﴾ [Al 'Imran: 113].

(153), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

As for the ummah of the followers, they are those who believe in the messengers, as He said: ﴿You are the best ummah brought forth for mankind﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110]. And in the Sahih: "Then I will say: My ummah, my ummah."

The word ummah is also used for a faction and a group, as in His words: ﴿And among the people of Moses is an ummah who guide by truth and by it act justly﴾ [al-A'raf: 159], and He said: ﴿Among the People of the Scripture is an upright ummah who recite the verses of Allah during the night, and they prostrate﴾ [Al 'Imran: 113].

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about man and the blameworthy qualities within him, except for those of His servants who are believers whom Allah has shown mercy. When hardship afflicts him after a blessing, he falls into despair and hopelessness regarding good in the future, and into ingratitude and denial regarding his past condition, as though he had never seen any good and did not hope for any relief afterward. Likewise, if a blessing reaches him after a calamity, ﴿he will surely say, "The evils have gone from me."﴾ That is, he says that no harm or misfortune will touch him after this. ﴿Indeed, he is exultant and boastful﴾: that is, he exults in what he has and is insolent and proud toward others.

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Except for those who are patient﴾ in hardships and adversities, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ in times of ease and well-being. ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾ for the harm that befalls them, ﴿and a great reward﴾ for what they had sent forward in times of ease.

As has come in the hadith: "By He in whose hand is my soul, no concern, grief, fatigue, illness, or sorrow afflicts the believer, not even a thorn that pricks him, except that Allah expiates some of his sins by it." [Muslim narrated something similar in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa'id (2573), and from the hadith of Abu Hurairah alone (2574).] And in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): "By He in whose hand is my soul, Allah does not decree for the believer any decree except that it is good for him. If prosperity reaches him and he is grateful, it is good for him; and if adversity reaches him and he is patient, it is good for him. This is not so for anyone except the believer." [Sahih Muslim, no. 299, with the wording: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all his affairs are good," from the hadith of Suhayb al-Rumi, may Allah be pleased with him; it is not in Sahih al-Bukhari.]

Likewise Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ [Surah al-Asr]. And Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious; when evil touches him, he is distressed; and when good touches him, he is withholding, except for those who pray﴾ [al-Ma'arij 70:19–22], and so on.

The Most High says, consoling His Messenger ﷺ regarding what the polytheists used to nitpick about him, in what they said about the Messenger. As He informed about them: ﴿They said, "What is this Messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him to be a warner with him, or a treasure not bestowed upon him, or a garden not given to him from which he could eat?" And the wrongdoers said, "You follow only a man bewitched."﴾ [Al-Furqan: 7, 8]. So Allah the Most High commanded His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and guided him not to let his chest be constricted by that from them, nor let it weaken him, nor let it turn him away from calling them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, at the hours of the night and the extremities of the day. As He the Most High said: ﴿And We certainly know that your chest is constricted by what they say. So exalt [Allah] with the praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate. And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty [death].﴾ [Al-Hijr: 97-99]. And here He said: ﴿Perhaps you are going to leave some of what is revealed to you and your chest is constricted by it because they say [that]...﴾, meaning: because of their saying that, "You are only a warner, and you have an example in your brothers, the messengers before you, for they were denied and harmed, and they were patient until the help of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, came to them."

Then the Most High explained the inimitability (i'jaz) of the Qur'an, and that mankind is not able to produce its like, nor ten surahs like it, nor a single surah like it, because the speech of the Lord is not resembled by the speech of created beings, just as His attributes do not resemble the attributes of created things, and His essence has nothing like it. He is exalted, sanctified, and transcendent; there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him.

Then He said: ﴿And if they do not respond to you﴾, meaning: if they do not bring a counter-example to what you have challenged them with, then know that they are incapable of that, and that this speech is sent down from Allah, comprising His knowledge, His command, and His prohibition. ﴿And that there is no deity except Him, so will you [now] submit?﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 11, verse 15–16:

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse: "Indeed, the people of showing-off (riya') are given their good deeds in this world, and that is because they will not be wronged even a speck (naqir). He says: whoever does a righteous deed seeking the worldly life, fasting, or prayer, or night vigil (tahajjud) at night, does it only seeking the worldly life, Allah says: I will pay him in full for what he sought in the world of reward, and his deed which he did seeking the worldly life is nullified, and in the Hereafter he is among the losers."

Similarly it was narrated from Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others besides them.

Anas ibn Malik and al-Hasan said: it was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians. Mujahid and others said: it was revealed concerning the people of showing-off (riya').

Qatadah said: whoever has the world as his concern, his zeal (sadam), his seeking, and his intention, Allah will reward him for his good deeds in this world, then he will arrive in the Hereafter with no good deed for which he is given a reward. As for the believer, he is rewarded for his good deeds in this world and is recompensed for them in the Hereafter.

A similar statement has been transmitted in a raised (marfu') hadith: [[The Hafiz is likely referring to the hadith narrated by al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani from Anas, whose wording is: "Whoever has the world as his aim and his zeal, and it is his sole concern, and for it he intends, Allah places poverty between his eyes, scatters his affairs upon him, and nothing comes to him from it except what has been written for him. And whoever has the Hereafter as his aim and his zeal, and it is his sole concern, and for it he intends, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, places richness in his heart, gathers his affairs upon him, and the world comes to him humbled." And al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (no. 2465) narrated it from Anas in a shorter form, and Ibn Majah in his Sunan narrated it from Zayd ibn Thabit as a raised hadith with similar meaning.]]

And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever desires the hastened [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We desire. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will enter, blamed and banished. And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its striving while he is a believer – those are the ones whose striving is appreciated. To each – these and those – We extend from the gift of your Lord. And the gift of your Lord has never been restricted. Look how We have preferred some of them over others, and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference.﴾ [Al-Isra': 18–21], [[In one manuscript: "what He wills".]] And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him from it, but he has no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [Al-Shura: 20].

And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever desires the hastened [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We desire. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will enter, blamed and banished. And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its striving while he is a believer – those are the ones whose striving is appreciated. To each – these and those – We extend from the gift of your Lord. And the gift of your Lord has never been restricted. Look how We have preferred some of them over others, and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference.﴾ [Al-Isra': 18–21], [[In one manuscript: "what He wills".]] And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him from it, but he has no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [Al-Shura: 20].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah the Exalted informs about the state of the believers, who are upon the fitrah (innate disposition) of Allah, which He instilled in His servants, namely acknowledging Him that there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30]

And in the two Sahihs, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, and then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1385) and Sahih Muslim no. (2658).]

And in Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Himar, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Allah the Exalted says: 'Indeed, I created My servants as hunafa' (upright monotheists), then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them.'" [Sahih Muslim no. (2865).]

And in the Musnad and the Sunan: "Every child is born upon this millah (religious community), until his tongue speaks for him," and the hadith continues. [Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (3/353) through Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from al-Hasan, from Jabir.]

So the believer remains upon this fitrah.

As for His saying: ﴿and there follows it a witness from Him﴾, meaning: there came to him a witness from Allah, which is what He revealed to the prophets of the pure, perfected, exalted laws, concluded with the law of Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and upon all of them. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Dahhak, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Suddi, and others said regarding His saying ﴿and there follows it a witness from Him﴾ that it is Jibril (peace be upon him).

And from 'Ali, al-Hasan, and Qatadah: it is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Both are close in meaning, because each of Jibril and Muhammad, may the blessings of Allah be upon them both, conveyed the message of Allah the Exalted: Jibril to Muhammad, and Muhammad to the Ummah.

It was also said: it is 'Ali. But this is weak, and no one of note holds it. The first and second views are the truth. That is because the believer has in his fitrah that which bears witness to the Shari'ah in general, while the details are taken from the Shari'ah, and the fitrah confirms it and believes in it. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord and there follows it a witness from Him﴾, which is the Qur'an, conveyed by Jibril to the Prophet (ﷺ), and conveyed by the Prophet Muhammad to his Ummah.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And before it was the Book of Musa﴾, meaning: before this Qur'an was the Book of Musa, which is the Torah, ﴿as a guide and mercy﴾, meaning: Allah the Exalted sent down to that nation a leader for them and a model they would follow, and a mercy from Allah toward them. Whoever believes in it with true belief, it leads him to belief in the Qur'an. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those believe in it﴾.

Then Allah the Exalted said, threatening those who deny the Qur'an or any part of it: ﴿And whoever of the sects disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾, meaning: whoever disbelieves in the Qur'an among all the people of the earth, its polytheists, People of the Book, and others, from all the groups of the children of Adam with their differing colors, forms, and races, of those to whom the Qur'an has reached, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [Al-An'am: 19], and He said: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [Al-A'raf: 158], and He said: ﴿And whoever of the sects disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place.﴾ In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, no one from this Ummah hears of me, whether Jew or Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he enters the Fire." [As stated; the hadith is in Sahih Muslim no. (153) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, and this chain was narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/281), Ahmad in his Musnad (4/396), and al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (8/261).]

Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani said, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "I never heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in its exact form without finding its confirmation—or he said its affirmation—in the Qur'an. It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'No one from this Ummah hears of me, nor any Jew or Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he enters the Fire.' So I began to say: Where is its confirmation in the Book of Allah? He said: Rarely did I hear from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without finding its affirmation in the Qur'an, until I found this verse: ﴿And whoever of the sects disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place.﴾" He said: "From all the religious communities." [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/280).]

His saying: ﴿So be not in doubt about it. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord﴾, meaning: the Qur'an is the truth from Allah; there is no doubt or uncertainty in it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The revelation of the Book, there is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [As-Sajdah: 1-2], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book; there is no doubt in it, [a guidance for those conscious of Allah]﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 1-2].

* *

His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you should strive, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾ [Al-An'am: 116], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a party of believers﴾ [Saba': 20].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah the Exalted describes the state of those who fabricate lies against Him and their disgrace in the Hereafter, before the assembled creation: the angels, the messengers, the prophets, and all of mankind and the jinn. As Imam Ahmad said:

Bahz and Affan narrated to us, saying: Hammam informed us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: "I was holding the hand of Ibn Umar when a man approached him and said: 'How did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speak about private conversation (najwa) on the Day of Resurrection?' He said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will bring the believer near, will place His covering (kanaf) over him, and will conceal him from the people. He will make him acknowledge his sins and will say to him: 'Do you recognize the sin of such-and-such? Do you recognize the sin of such-and-such? Do you recognize the sin of such-and-such?' until, when He has made him acknowledge his sins and he thinks within himself that he is ruined, He will say: 'I have covered them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.' Then he will be given the record of his good deeds. As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, they will be called: ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Surely, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾."'"

They will abide therein forever. They will not die, grow old, or fall ill. They will sleep without covering themselves, and they will neither spit nor blow their noses. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being opposed﴾ [al-Anfal: 23]. As for the believer, he is perceptive, intelligent, and discerning, seeing the truth and distinguishing it from falsehood. He follows good and abandons evil. He hears the proof and differentiates it from doubt, so falsehood does not deceive him. Can these two be equal?

﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ That is, will you not take heed and distinguish between these and those? As He said in another verse: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of the Garden are not equal. The companions of the Garden are the triumphant﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]. And He said: ﴿The blind and the seeing are not alike, nor are the darknesses and the light, nor the shade and the scorching heat. Nor are the living and the dead alike. Indeed, Allah causes whom He wills to hear, but you cannot make those in the graves hear. You are only a warner. Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir: 19–24].

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the state of the wretched, He followed it with mention of the blessed (al-su'ada'), who are those who believed and did righteous deeds. Their hearts believed, and their limbs acted righteously, in both word and deed, by performing acts of obedience and abstaining from what is forbidden. Through this they inherited the Gardens, which contain lofty chambers, arranged couches, hanging clusters of fruit, raised carpets, beautiful and virtuous companions, varied fruits, desirable foods, delicious drinks, and gazing upon the Creator of the earth and the heavens. They will abide therein forever. They will not die, grow old, or fall ill. They will sleep without covering themselves, and they will neither spit nor blow their noses. Their only emission will be a sweat of musk.

Then Allah, exalted is He, set forth the parable of the disbelievers and the believers. He said: ﴿The likeness of the two groups﴾, that is, those He described first as wretched and the believers as blessed. The former are like the blind and the deaf, and the latter are like the seeing and the hearing. The disbeliever is blind to the face of the truth in this world, and in the Hereafter he will not be guided to any good nor recognize it. Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 11, verses 25–27:

He, exalted is He, informs about Nuh (peace be upon him), who was the first messenger sent by God to the people of the earth among the polytheists, the worshippers of idols, that he said to his people: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a clear warner﴾, meaning: manifestly warning you of the punishment of God if you worship other than God. For this reason he said: ﴿that you worship none but God﴾. And his saying ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day﴾ means: if you persist in what you are upon, God will punish you with a painful, afflicting, grievous punishment in the Hereafter.

﴿So the eminent ones among his people who disbelieved said﴾. The malaʾ (eminent ones, the chiefs and the great ones) are the leaders and the elders among the disbelievers. They said: ﴿We see you only as a human being like ourselves﴾, meaning: you are not an angel, but you are a human being, so how can revelation be sent to you over us? Then: ﴿And we see none following you except those who are our lowest (arādhilunā), such as the tradesmen and the weavers and their like, and the nobles and the leaders from among us did not follow you.﴾ Then these who followed you did not do so after deliberation, reflection or consideration, but merely upon your calling them, they answered you and followed you. For this reason he said: ﴿And we see none following you except those who are our lowest, at first sight (bādiya al-ra'y)﴾, meaning: at the very first glance. ﴿And we see in you no merit over us﴾: they say, we have seen no virtue for you over us, in creation or in character, nor in provision or condition, since you entered this religion of yours. ﴿Rather, we think you are liars﴾, meaning: in what you claim for yourselves of righteousness, piety, worship and happiness in the Hereafter when you arrive there.

This is the objection of the disbelievers against Nuh (peace be upon him) and his followers, and it is evidence of their ignorance and their lack of knowledge and understanding, for the lowliness of those who follow the truth is no disgrace to the truth, since the truth in itself is sound, whether the nobles or the lowly follow it. Indeed, the truth beyond doubt is that the followers of the truth are the noble, even if they are poor, and those who reject it are the lowly, even if they are rich. Moreover, it is generally the case that those who follow the truth are the weak among people, while the nobles and the great are usually opposed to it, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And thus We did not send before you any warner into a town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 23]. When Heraclius, the king of the Romans, asked Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb about the qualities of the Prophet ﷺ, he said to him, among what he said: "Did the nobles of the people follow him, or their weak?" He replied: "Rather, their weak." Heraclius said: "They are the followers of the messengers."

* *

Their saying ﴿at first sight (bādiya al-ra'y)﴾ is not a reproach or a defect, because when the truth becomes clear, there is no room left for deliberation (tarawwī) or thought; rather, it is necessary for every person of purity and intelligence to follow the truth in such a state, and only one who is incapable or dull would pause and hesitate here. The messengers, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them all, came only with a matter that is evident and clear.

It has come in a hadith that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I have never invited anyone to Islam except that he had some hesitation (kabwa), except Abu Bakr, for he did not falter (lam yatalaʿthama)." [Mentioned by the author in al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya (3/27) from Ibn Ishaq, and it is mursal (disconnected).] That is: he did not hesitate nor deliberate, because he saw a matter that was great, clear and manifest, so he hastened to it and rushed toward it.

* *

Their saying: ﴿And we see in you no merit over us﴾ — they do not see that, because they are blind to the truth, they do not hear nor see. Rather, they are in their doubt hesitating, wandering in the darkness of ignorance. They are the liars and the fabricators, the fewest and the lowest, and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers.

Allah, the Exalted, says, relating what Noah replied to his people on this matter: ﴿Tell me, if I am upon clear proof from my Lord﴾, meaning: upon certainty and a manifest matter, and a true prophethood, which is a great mercy from Allah to him and to them. ﴿But it has been concealed from you﴾, meaning: it has been hidden from you, so you did not perceive it, nor did you recognize its worth, rather you hastened to deny and reject it. ﴿Shall we compel you to accept it while you are averse to it?﴾ meaning: shall we force you to accept it while you dislike it? [[In one manuscript: "nughdabkum" (we would anger you).]]

He says to his people: "I do not ask you for wealth in return for my counsel to you; I seek no wage from you. I seek my reward only from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed﴾. It is as though they had asked him to drive the believers away from him, out of disdain and a sense of their own high status, being unwilling to sit with them. This is like what their counterparts asked of the Seal of the Messengers (ﷺ): that he drive away from them a group of the weak and sit with them in a special assembly. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾ [al-An'am: 52], and ﴿Restrain yourself to be with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and do not let your eyes pass beyond them﴾ [al-Kahf: 28]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53], and so on, the verses.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 11, verse 31:

He informs them that he is a messenger from Allah, calling to the worship of Allah alone, without any partner, by Allah's permission granted to him in that matter. He does not ask them for any wage for it; rather, he calls whoever he meets, whether noble or lowly, and whoever responds to him has indeed been saved. [He also informs them]¹ that he has no power to dispose of the treasures of Allah, and he knows of the unseen only what Allah has made him aware of. He is not an angel among the angels, but a human messenger, supported by miracles.

﴿And I do not say to you about those whom you despise and look down upon: Allah will never grant them any good.﴾ [I do not say that] they have no reward with Allah for their faith. Allah knows best what is within their souls. If they are believers inwardly, as is the apparent state of their condition, then for them is the best reward [al-husna]. And if any human were to pronounce judgment on them after they had believed, he would be a wrongdoer, saying what he has no knowledge of.

¹ In one manuscript: "And he informs them."

Allah, exalted is He, says, reporting about the haste of Noah's people for the vengeance, punishment and wrath of Allah, and calamity is entrusted to speech: ﴿They said, "O Noah, you have argued with us and multiplied our arguments."﴾ That is, you disputed with us and went on at great length about it. ﴿And we will not follow you. So bring us what you threaten us with.﴾ That is, the vengeance and punishment. ﴿Invoke against us whatever you wish, and let come to us what you call down upon us, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [[In (ta): "man tad'unahu" (whom you invoke), and in (a): "bi-da'watihi" (by his supplication).]] He said, ﴿Only Allah will bring it to you if He wills, and you will not escape.﴾ That is, the one who punishes you and hastens it upon you is Allah, whom nothing can render powerless. ﴿And my advice will not benefit you, if I wanted to advise you, if Allah wills to lead you astray.﴾ That is, what benefit will my conveying to you, my warning you, and my advice do you, if Allah wills to lead you astray and to destroy you? ﴿He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ That is, He is the owner of the reins of affairs, the one who disposes of them, the just Judge who does not oppress. To Him belongs the creation and the command, and He is the Originator and the Restorer, the owner of this world and the Hereafter. [[In (ta): "al-mutasarrif" (the one who disposes).]]

This is a parenthetical statement placed in the middle of this narrative, confirming it and establishing its matter. Allah says to Muhammad (ﷺ): Or do these disbelievers, the deniers, say: "He has fabricated it and invented it from himself"? ﴿Say: If I have fabricated it, then upon me is my crime﴾, meaning, the sin of that would be upon me, ﴿and I am innocent of what you commit﴾, meaning: it is not invented or fabricated, because I know what Allah has of punishment for whoever lies against Him.

The Exalted informs that He revealed to Nuh when his people hastened on the vengeance of Allah upon them and His punishment for them. So Nuh invoked against them with his supplication, about which Allah, Exalted is He, reported that he said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant.﴾ [Nuh: 26] ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overcome, so give victory."﴾ [al-Qamar: 10] At that point Allah, Exalted is He, revealed to him: ﴿None will believe among your people except those who have already believed.﴾ So do not grieve over them, and let not their affair distress you.

﴿And construct the ship﴾, meaning the ark, ﴿under Our eyes﴾, meaning within Our sight, ﴿and Our inspiration﴾, meaning and Our instruction to you about what you should make. ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged. Indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾

Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: Allah commanded him to plant the wood, cut it, and dry it, and that took a hundred years, and shaping it took another hundred years. It was said: forty years. And Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq reported from the Torah that Allah commanded him to make it from teak wood, and that its length should be eighty cubits and its width fifty cubits.

And that he should coat its inside and outside with pitch, and that he should make for it a jutting prow that cuts through the water.

Qatadah said: its length was three hundred cubits, with a width of fifty.

From al-Hasan: its length was six hundred cubits and its width three hundred cubits.

From him, together with Ibn Abbas: its length was one thousand two hundred cubits, with a width of six hundred.

It was also said: its length was two thousand cubits and its width one hundred cubits. And Allah knows best.

They all said: its height above the water was thirty cubits, in three decks, each deck ten cubits. The lowest was for the animals and wild beasts, the middle for humans, and the highest for birds. Its door was in its side, and it had a covering over the top that was sealed upon it.

The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) cited a strange report (athar) from the narration of Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that he said: The disciples (al-Hawariyyun) said to Isa ibn Maryam: "If you were to send us a man who witnessed the ship, so that he could tell us about it." He said: So he set off with them until he reached a heap of earth. He took a handful of that earth in his palm and said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the grave of Ham ibn Nuh." He said: And he struck the heap with his staff and said: "Rise by the permission of Allah," and behold, he was standing, shaking the dust from his head, and he had grown white-haired. Isa, peace be upon him, said to him: "Is this how you died?" He said: "No. Rather I died while I was young, but I thought it was the Hour, so for that reason I turned grey." He said: "Tell us about the ship of Nuh." He said: Its length was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its width six hundred cubits, and it had three decks: one deck had the animals and wild beasts, one deck had the humans, and one deck had the birds. When the droppings of the animals increased, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Nuh, peace be upon him, to "rub the tail of the elephant," and he rubbed it, and from it there fell a male pig and a female pig, and they went to the dung. When the mouse fell upon the ship's timbers, gnawing at them and its ropes, Allah revealed to Nuh, "Strike between the eyes of the lion," and from its nostril there came out a male cat and a female cat, and they went for the mouse. Isa, peace be upon him, said to him: "How did Nuh know that the lands had been drowned?" He said: "He sent the crow to bring him the news, and it found a carcass and settled upon it, so he invoked fear upon it, and for that reason it does not frequent houses." He said: "Then he sent the dove, and it came back with an olive leaf in its beak and mud on its feet, and he knew that the lands had been drowned." He said: "So he bound it with the green collar around its neck, and invoked that it would be in comfort and safety, and for that reason it frequents houses." He said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not take him to our families so that he may sit with us and tell us?" He said: "How will one who has no provision follow you?" He said: So he said to him: "Return by the permission of Allah," and he returned to dust.

Indeed, it is as Allah Most High said: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth, and We caused the earth to gush forth with springs, and the waters met according to a matter already decreed. As for His words, ﴿and the oven overflowed﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: "al-tannur" (the oven) means the surface of the earth. That is, the earth became gushing springs, until the water boiled up from the ovens, which are the places of fire, and they began to boil with water. This is the view of the majority of the early generations (al-Salaf) and the scholars of later generations (al-Khalaf).

And from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: "al-tannur" means the splitting of the morning, the illumination of dawn, and its light and brightness.

The first view is more apparent.

Mujahid and al-Sha'bi said: this oven was in Kufa. And from Ibn 'Abbas: it was a spring in India. And from Qatadah: it was a spring in al-Jazirah, called 'Ayn al-Wardah.

These are strange opinions.

Then Allah commanded Nuh, peace be upon him, to carry with him in the ship two of every pair, from the various kinds of living creatures, and it is said also other plants, two: a male and a female. It is said that the first of the birds to be admitted was the dove (al-Durrah), and the last of the animals to be admitted was the donkey. It is reported that Iblis entered clinging to its tail. He entered with his hand, and when he wanted to rise, Iblis, clinging to its tail, weighed him down. Nuh kept saying to him: "What is wrong with you? Woe to you! Enter!" But he would rise and could not. So he said: "Enter, even if Iblis is with you," and they both entered the ship.

Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud mentioned that they were unable to carry the lion with them, until fever was cast upon it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to me, Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Nuh carried in the ship two of every pair, his companions said: 'How can the cattle be at ease (or: be at ease) with the lion among them?' So Allah sent fever upon it, and it was the first fever to descend upon the earth. Then they complained about the mouse, saying: 'The little rodent is spoiling our food and our goods.' So Allah inspired the lion, and it sneezed, and the cat came out of it, and the mouse hid from it."

[This is a mursal report, and other reports concerning Nuh's ship have come down other than what the Hafiz mentioned, most of them through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. Ibn Hibban said: "He was among those who would invert reports, to the extent that this became common in his narrations, raising mursal reports and attributing mawquf reports, so he deserved to be abandoned." Among what he narrated about Nuh's ship is what Ibn Hajar cited in al-Tahdhib (6/179) from al-Saji, who said: al-Rabi' narrated to us, al-Shafi'i narrated to us, who said: 'It was said to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd: Did your father narrate to you from your grandfather that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the ship of Nuh circled the House and prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam"?' He said: 'Yes.' And a man mentioned to Malik a disconnected report, and he said: 'Go to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, who will narrate to you from his father, from Nuh!!' See also the book: al-Isra'iliyyat fi Kutub al-Tafsir by Muhammad Abu Shahbah (p. 218).]

* *

As for His words, ﴿and your family, except those against whom the word has already preceded﴾, meaning: "Carry in it your family, namely the people of your household and relatives," except those among them against whom the word has already preceded, those who did not believe in Allah. Among them was his son Yam, who isolated himself alone, and the wife of Nuh, who was a disbeliever in Allah and His Messenger.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and those who believed﴾, meaning: from your people, ﴿but none believed with him except a few﴾, meaning: a small, insignificant number, despite the long duration and his staying among them for a thousand years less fifty years. From Ibn 'Abbas: they were eighty persons, including their women. From Ka'b al-Ahbar: they were seventy-two persons. It was also said: they were ten. And it was said: they were only Nuh and his sons, the three: Sam, Ham and Yafith, and the four daughters-in-law, the wives of these three, and the wife of Yam. It was also said: rather, the wife of Nuh was with them in the ship, but this is open to question; rather, the apparent view is that she perished, because she was upon the religion of her people, so what befell them befell her, just as what befell the people of Lut befell the wife of Lut. And Allah knows best and is most wise.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 11, verses 41–43:

Allah, exalted is He, says, reporting about Noah, peace be upon him, that he said to those whom he was commanded to carry with him in the ship: ﴿Embark upon it; in the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring﴾. That is: in the name of Allah is its running upon the surface of the water, and in the name of Allah is the end of its journey, which is its anchoring.

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi recited: "Bismillahi mujriha wa mursiha" ("In the name of Allah is its causing it to run and its causing it to anchor").

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when you have settled, you and whoever is with you, upon the ship, say: "All praise is due to Allah, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people." And say: "My Lord, let me land at a blessed landing place, and You are the best of those who bring to land."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 23:28–29]. For this reason, invoking the name of Allah (tasmiyah) is recommended at the beginning of matters: when boarding a ship and when mounting an animal, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and the cattle that which you ride, so that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon them and say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we were not capable of that. And indeed, to our Lord we will return."﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 43:12–14]. The Sunnah has also come urging this and recommending it, as will come in Surah Az-Zukhruf, Allah willing, and in Him is trust.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim al-Baghawi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, and Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Sajji narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi narrated to us, the two of them saying: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn al-Hasan al-Hilali narrated to us, from Nahshal ibn Sa'id, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The security of my Ummah from drowning, when they board ships, is that they say: 'In the name of Allah, the King,' ﴿And they did not appraise Allah with His true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him﴾ [Az-Zumar 39:67], ﴿In the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾."[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/124). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/132): "In it is Nahshal ibn Sa'id, who is abandoned (matruk)."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ is fitting when mentioning the punishment of the disbelievers by drowning them all. It is mentioned that He is Forgiving and Merciful, as He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Al-A'raf 7:167], and He said: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 13:6], and other verses in which He combines His retribution with His mercy.

* *

His saying: ﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains﴾, that is, the ship was moving with them upon the surface of the water, which had covered all the earth, until it rose above the peaks of the mountains, and it rose above them by fifteen cubits. It was said: by eighty miles. This ship, upon the surface of the water, was moving by the permission of Allah, under His protection, care, guardianship, and favor, as He said: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship, to make it for you a reminder and for a retaining ear to retain it﴾ [Al-Haqqah 69:11–12], and He said: ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails, running under Our eyes, as a reward for one who had been disbelieved. And We left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [Al-Qamar 54:13–15].

* *

His saying: ﴿And Noah called to his son, who was apart, "O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers."﴾ This was the fourth son, and his name was "Yam," and he was a disbeliever. His father invited him, at the time of boarding the ship, to believe and to board with them and not to drown like the disbelievers drowned. ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water."﴾ It was said that he made for himself a vessel of glass, but this is from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives taken from Israelite sources), and Allah knows best its authenticity. What the Qur'an explicitly states is that he said: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾; in his ignorance he believed that the flood would not reach the peaks of the mountains, and that if he clung to the top of a mountain, that would save him from drowning. So his father Noah, peace be upon him, said to him: ﴿There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for whom He has mercy﴾, that is: nothing protects today from the command of Allah. It was also said that "ʿāṣim" here carries the meaning of "maʿṣūm" (one who is protected), as it is said "ṭāʿim" and "kāsin" in the sense of "maṭʿūm" (one who is fed) and "maksū" (one who is clothed). ﴿And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 11, verses 41–43:

Allah, exalted is He, says, reporting about Noah, peace be upon him, that he said to those whom he was commanded to carry with him in the ship: ﴿Embark upon it; in the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring﴾. That is: in the name of Allah is its running upon the surface of the water, and in the name of Allah is the end of its journey, which is its anchoring.

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi recited: "Bismillahi mujriha wa mursiha" ("In the name of Allah is its causing it to run and its causing it to anchor").

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when you have settled, you and whoever is with you, upon the ship, say: "All praise is due to Allah, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people." And say: "My Lord, let me land at a blessed landing place, and You are the best of those who bring to land."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 23:28–29]. For this reason, invoking the name of Allah (tasmiyah) is recommended at the beginning of matters: when boarding a ship and when mounting an animal, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and the cattle that which you ride, so that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon them and say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we were not capable of that. And indeed, to our Lord we will return."﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 43:12–14]. The Sunnah has also come urging this and recommending it, as will come in Surah Az-Zukhruf, Allah willing, and in Him is trust.
