The Lord, exalted is He, informs us that when the people of the earth drowned, all except those on the ship, He commanded the earth to swallow its water, which had gushed forth from it and gathered upon it, and He commanded the sky to cease its rain. ﴿And the water subsided﴾ means it began to decrease. ﴿And the matter was decided﴾ means that the people of the earth, all of them, of those who disbelieved in Allah, were finished off, so that not a single dwelling-place remained of them. ﴿And it came to rest﴾ means the ship, with those who were in it, ﴿upon al-Judi﴾. Mujahid said: it is a mountain in al-Jazirah. On that day the mountains rose high and grew tall above the flood, while al-Judi humbled itself before Allah, mighty and majestic, so it did not drown, and the ship of Noah, peace be upon him, came to rest upon it.

Qatadah said: the ship remained upon it for a month, until they disembarked from it. Qatadah said: Allah left the ship of Noah, peace be upon him, upon al-Judi in the land of al-Jazirah as a lesson and a sign, until the earliest of this Ummah saw it. And how many ships have been after it that were destroyed and turned to ashes.

Al-Dahhak said: al-Judi is a mountain at Mosul. Others said: it is Mount Sinai (al-Tur).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Amr ibn Rafi' narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Tawbah ibn Salim, who said: I saw Zirr ibn Hubaysh praying in the corner when one enters through the Kindah gates, on your right. I asked him: "Do you pray so much here on Friday?" He said: "It has reached me that the ship of Noah came to rest here."

Ilba' ibn Ahmad said, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: There were eighty men with Noah in the ship, along with their families, and they remained in the ship for one hundred and fifty days. Allah directed the ship to Makkah, and it circled the House for forty days. Then Allah directed it to al-Judi, and it settled upon it. Noah sent out the crow to bring him news of the earth, but it went off and alighted upon the carrion and delayed. So he sent the dove, which came back to him with an olive leaf, and its feet were smeared with mud. Noah, peace be upon him, knew that the water had receded. He descended to the foot of al-Judi and built a town, and named it Thamanin (Eighty). One day they woke up and their tongues had become confused into eighty languages, one of which is the Arabic tongue. Some of them could not understand the speech of others, and Noah, peace be upon him, would interpret for them.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: the ship circled between the east and the west before it came to rest upon al-Judi.

Qatadah and others said: they embarked on the tenth of the month of Rajab, sailed for one hundred and fifty days, and came to rest with them upon al-Judi for a month. Their disembarking from the ship was on the day of 'Ashura' in Muharram. Something similar to this has come in a raised (marfu') hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir (Tafsir al-Tabari 15/335), and it is fabricated. They also fasted that day. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, Abd al-Samad ibn Habib al-Azdi narrated to us, from his father Habib ibn Abd Allah, from Shubayl, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by some Jews who were fasting on the day of 'Ashura'. He said: "What is this fast?" They said: "This is the day on which Allah saved Musa and the Children of Israel from drowning, and Pharaoh drowned, and this is the day on which the ship came to rest upon al-Judi. So Noah and Musa, peace be upon them both, fasted it in thanks to Allah, mighty and majestic." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have more right to Musa than you, and more right to fasting this day." So he fasted it, and he said to his companions: "Whoever among you has begun the day fasting, let him complete his fast, and whoever has eaten, let him complete the rest of his day." [Al-Musnad (2/359)]

This is a strange (gharib) hadith from this route, but part of it has a witness in the Sahih: in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4680, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Madinah and the Jews were fasting 'Ashura'. They said: "This is a day on which Musa prevailed over Pharaoh." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "You have more right to Musa than they do, so fast."

* *

His saying: ﴿And it was said: Away with the wrongdoing people﴾ means: destruction and loss for them, and distance from the mercy of Allah, for they were utterly destroyed, so that none of them remained.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir and the scholar Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim have related, in their two tafsirs, from the hadith of Musa ibn Ya'qub al-Zam'i, from Qa'id, the freedman of Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', that Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Rabi'ah informed him that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), informed him that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If Allah had shown mercy to anyone of the people of Noah, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Noah, peace be upon him, remained among his people for a thousand years [minus fifty years], that is, and he planted trees for a hundred years, and they grew tall and took every shape. Then he cut them and made them into a ship, and they would pass by him, mocking him and saying: 'You are making a ship on dry land, how will it sail?' He said: 'You will know.' When he finished and the water gushed forth and reached the alleys, the mother of the child feared for him, for she loved him intensely, so she went out to the mountain until she reached its third. When the water reached her, she rose until she reached two-thirds of it. When the water reached her, she carried him out until she stood upon the mountain. When it reached her neck, she lifted him up with her two hands, and they both drowned. So if Allah had shown mercy to anyone of them, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child."

This is a strange hadith from this route. The story of this child and his mother has also been related from Ka'b al-Ahbar and Mujahid ibn Jabr in a similar form.

This is a question of inquiry and seeking clarification from Noah, peace be upon him, about the condition of his son who drowned. ﴿So Noah called out to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family"﴾ — meaning: and You had promised me the salvation of my family, and Your promise is the truth that is not broken, so how did he drown while You are the most just of judges? ﴿He said, "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family"﴾ — meaning: those whose salvation I had promised; for indeed I promised you the salvation of those of your family who believed. For this reason He said: ﴿except for those against whom the Word has already gone forth﴾ [Hud: 40]. So this son was among those against whom the Word had gone forth regarding drowning, because of his disbelief and his opposition to his father, the Prophet of Allah Noah, peace be upon him.

Several of the imams have explicitly stated the error of those who held, in interpreting this, that he was not his son but was rather the son of an adulteress (ibn zina). It is related that the view that he was not his son, but was the son of his wife, is reported from Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ubayd ibn Umayr, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, and Ibn Jurayj. Some of them argued with the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, his deed is unrighteous﴾ and with His words: ﴿but they betrayed them﴾ [at-Tahrim: 10]. Among those who said this was al-Hasan al-Basri, who argued with these two verses. Some of them say: he was the son of his wife. This may be what he intended, as al-Hasan intended, or he meant that he was attributed to him figuratively, because he was a stepson (rabib) in his household. And Allah knows best.

Ibn 'Abbas and several of the early scholars (salaf) said: "The wife of a prophet never committed adultery at all." He said: and His words, ﴿indeed, he is not of your family﴾, mean: those whose salvation I had promised you.

The saying of Ibn 'Abbas on this is the truth from which there is no escape, for Allah, glorified is He, is too jealous to allow the wife of a prophet to commit such an indecency. For this reason Allah was angry with those who slandered Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'ishah, daughter of as-Siddiq, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and He rebuked the believers who spoke of this and spread it. For this reason the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a faction among you. Do not consider it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what he has earned of sin, and he who undertook the greater portion thereof—for him is a great punishment﴾ up to His words ﴿when you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge, and you thought it trivial, while it was great in the sight of Allah﴾ [an-Nur: 11–15].

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah and others, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He was his son, except that he opposed him in deed and intention." Ikrimah said: in some readings: "Indeed, he did an unrighteous deed," and betrayal can be in ways other than one.

It has been reported in a hadith that the Messenger of Allah recited it that way. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reading: 'Indeed, he did an unrighteous deed,'" and I heard him say: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [az-Zumar: 53] [Musnad (6/454)].

Ahmad also said: Waki' narrated to us, Harun an-Nahwi narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah that the Messenger of Allah recited it: "Indeed, he did an unrighteous deed" [Musnad (6/294)].

Ahmad repeated it also in his Musnad [Musnad (6/322)].

Umm Salamah is "Hind," Umm al-Mu'minin, and the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that it is Asma' bint Yazid, for she is also known by that kunyah. [al-Tabari said in his tafsir (15/348): "We do not know of anyone among the readers of the cities who recited this reading except some later scholars, who relied on a report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he recited it thus, which is not of sound chain, which is a hadith narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who sometimes says 'from Umm Salamah' and sometimes says 'from Asma' bint Yazid,' and we do not know whether Yazid had a daughter named that, nor do we know that Shahr's hearing from Umm Salamah is authentic." See the marginal notes of Ustadh Mahmud Shakir on it, which are beneficial and excellent.]

'Abd al-Razzaq also said: al-Thawri and Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sulayman ibn Qatah, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas—he was asked—while he was beside the Ka'bah, about the words of Allah: ﴿but they betrayed them﴾ [at-Tahrim: 10]. He said: "Indeed, it was not by fornication, but this one (the wife) would inform the people that he (the husband) was mad, and that one (the wife) would point out the guests." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, he did an unrighteous deed﴾. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: Ammar al-Dhuhabi informed me that he asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about that, and he said: "He was the son of Noah. Indeed Allah does not lie!" He said: ﴿And Noah called out to his son﴾. He said: Some of the scholars said: "No wife of a prophet ever committed fornication" [narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (15/343)].

Similarly it is reported from Mujahid also, and Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Maymun ibn Mihran, and Thabit ibn al-Hajjaj, and it is the preference of Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, and it is the correct view, without any doubt.

Some of them argued with the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, his deed is unrighteous﴾ and with His words: ﴿but they betrayed them﴾ [at-Tahrim: 10]. Among those who said this was al-Hasan al-Basri, who argued with these two verses. Some of them say: he was the son of his wife. This may be what he intended, as al-Hasan intended, or he meant that he was attributed to him figuratively, because he was a stepson (rabib) in his household. And Allah knows best.

Ibn 'Abbas and several of the early scholars (salaf) said: "The wife of a prophet never committed adultery at all." He said: and His words, ﴿indeed, he is not of your family﴾, mean: those whose salvation I had promised you.

The saying of Ibn 'Abbas on this is the truth from which there is no escape, for Allah, glorified is He, is too jealous to allow the wife of a prophet to commit such an indecency. For this reason Allah was angry with those who slandered Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'ishah, daughter of as-Siddiq, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and He rebuked the believers who spoke of this and spread it. For this reason the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a faction among you. Do not consider it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what he has earned of sin, and he who undertook the greater portion thereof—for him is a great punishment﴾ up to His words ﴿when you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge, and you thought it trivial, while it was great in the sight of Allah﴾ [an-Nur: 11–15].

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah and others, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He was his son, except that he opposed him in deed and intention." Ikrimah said: in some readings: "Indeed, he did an unrighteous deed," and betrayal can be in ways other than one.

It has been reported in a hadith that the Messenger of Allah recited it that way. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reading: 'Indeed, he did an unrighteous deed,'" and I heard him say: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [az-Zumar: 53] [Musnad (6/454)].

Ahmad also said: Waki' narrated to us, Harun an-Nahwi narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah that the Messenger of Allah recited it: "Indeed, he did an unrighteous deed" [Musnad (6/294)].

Ahmad repeated it also in his Musnad [Musnad (6/322)].

Umm Salamah is "Hind," Umm al-Mu'minin, and the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that it is Asma' bint Yazid, for she is also known by that kunyah. [al-Tabari said in his tafsir (15/348): "We do not know of anyone among the readers of the cities who recited this reading except some later scholars, who relied on a report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he recited it thus, which is not of sound chain, which is a hadith narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who sometimes says 'from Umm Salamah' and sometimes says 'from Asma' bint Yazid,' and we do not know whether Yazid had a daughter named that, nor do we know that Shahr's hearing from Umm Salamah is authentic." See the marginal notes of Ustadh Mahmud Shakir on it, which are beneficial and excellent.]

'Abd al-Razzaq also said: al-Thawri and Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sulayman ibn Qatah, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas—he was asked—while he was beside the Ka'bah, about the words of Allah: ﴿but they betrayed them﴾ [at-Tahrim: 10]. He said: "Indeed, it was not by fornication, but this one (the wife) would inform the people that he (the husband) was mad, and that one (the wife) would point out the guests." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, he did an unrighteous deed﴾. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: Ammar al-Dhuhabi informed me that he asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about that, and he said: "He was the son of Noah. Indeed Allah does not lie!" He said: ﴿And Noah called out to his son﴾. He said: Some of the scholars said: "No wife of a prophet ever committed fornication" [narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (15/343)].

Similarly it is reported from Mujahid also, and Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Maymun ibn Mihran, and Thabit ibn al-Hajjaj, and it is the preference of Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, and it is the correct view, without any doubt.

[And his words]

Allah the Exalted informs of what was said to Nuh (peace be upon him) when the ship came to rest on al-Judi: a greeting of peace from Him upon him, and upon those believers who were with him, and upon every believer of his descendants until the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "Every believing man and woman until the Day of Resurrection entered into this greeting of peace. Likewise, every disbeliever, man and woman, until the Day of Resurrection entered into the punishment and the enjoyment of worldly life."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "When He willed to hold back the Flood, He sent a wind over the surface of the earth, and the water subsided, and the springs of the earth, the great abyss [[قال الأستاذ محمود شاكر في حاشيته على الطبري (١٥/٢٣٩) : "هكذا في المخطوطة والمطبوعة: "الغمر الأكبر". وأنا أرجح أنه خطأ محض، وأن الصواب: "الغوط الأكبر" وبهذا اللفظ رواه صاحب اللسان في مادة (غوط) ".]] and the gates of heaven were closed. Allah the Exalted [[في ت، أ: "يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لِنَبِيِّهِ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ".]] says: ﴿And it was said: "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold," and the water subsided, the matter was decided, and it came to rest upon al-Judi, and it was said: "Away with the wrongdoing people."﴾ [[زيادة من ت، أ، وفي هـ: "الآية".]] So the water kept decreasing, subsiding and receding. The resting of the ship upon al-Judi, as the People of the Torah (al-Tawrah) claim, took place in the seventh month, on the seventeenth night of it, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains were seen. After forty days had passed, Nuh opened the window of the ship that he had [[في ت، أ: "صنع".]] built, then he sent out the raven to see what the water had done, but it did not return to him. Then he sent the dove, and it returned to him, finding no place for its feet, so he stretched out his hand to the dove, took it, and brought it in. Then seven days passed, and he sent it out again to look for him. It returned at evening, and in its beak was an olive leaf [[في ت: "زيتونة".]], so Nuh knew that the water had receded from the face of the earth. Then he waited seven days, and it did not return, so Nuh knew that the earth had come out. When the year was complete from the time Allah sent the Flood until Nuh sent the dove, and one day of the first month of the second year had come, the face of the earth was exposed and the dry ground [[في ت: "النسر"، وفي أ: "البشر".]] appeared, and Nuh uncovered the covering of the ship and saw the face of the earth. In the second month of the second year, on the twenty-seventh night of it: ﴿It was said: "O Nuh, descend with peace from Us [and blessings upon you and upon the nations among those who are with you]"﴾ [[زيادة من ت، أ.]] [to the end of] [[زيادة من ت، أ.]] the verse [[تفسير الطبري (١٥/٣٣٨) .]].

Allah says to His Prophet [and Messenger Muhammad] (ﷺ): This story and others like it are "from the news of the unseen," meaning: from reports of past unseen matters, which We reveal to you in their true form and make clear to you, as if you were witnessing them. "We reveal them to you": that is, We inform you of them by revelation from Us to you. "You did not know them, neither you nor your people, before this": that is, neither you nor anyone among your people had knowledge of them, so that whoever denies you could say that you learned them from someone else. Rather, Allah informed you of them in conformity with what the true state of affairs was, as the books of the prophets before you bear witness. So be patient over the denial of those among your people who deny you and over their harm to you, for indeed We will support you (we will aid you and surround you with Our care) and make the final outcome yours and that of your followers in this world and the Hereafter, just as We did with your brothers among the messengers when We gave them victory over their enemies. "Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand, the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode" [Ghafir 40:51-52]. And Allah says: "And We had already decreed Our word to Our servants, the messengers: indeed, they would be the ones given victory, and indeed, Our soldiers would be the victorious" [As-Saffat 37:171-173]. And Allah says: "So be patient; indeed, the best outcome is for the righteous" [Hud 11:49].

Allah the Exalted says: "And We sent to 'Ad their brother Hud" (﴿إِلَى عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُودًا﴾), commanding them to worship Allah alone, with no partner, and forbidding them from worshipping the idols which they had invented and to which they had given the names of gods. He informed them that he did not seek from them any wage for this counsel and this conveyance from Allah: "Indeed, my reward is only from the One who created me" (﴿إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي﴾ is implied). Then he said, "Will you not then reason?" (﴿أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾), meaning: will you not understand who is calling you to that which benefits you in this world and the Hereafter, without any wage or reward?

Then he commanded them to seek forgiveness (istighfar), which expiates past sins, and to repent (tawbah) from what they would do in the future. Whoever is characterized by this attribute, Allah makes his provision easy for him, facilitates his affairs, and protects his condition and his strength. For this reason He said: "He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain" (﴿يُرْسِلِ السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْرَارًا﴾) [Nuh: 11], and as has come in the hadith: "Whoever persists in seeking forgiveness, Allah will grant him a way out of every distress, a relief from every hardship, and will provide for him from where he does not expect."

Ibn Kathir says: Allah, the Exalted, reports about the people of Hud that they said to their Prophet: "You have brought us no clear proof (bayyinah)," that is, no argument (hujjah), no indication (dalalah), and no demonstrative proof (burhan) for what you claim. "And we will not abandon our gods because of your words," that is, we will not leave them merely because you say, "Leave them," and "we are not going to believe you," that is, we will not accept you as truthful. "We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil," they mean: we think that some of the gods have afflicted you with madness and a derangement of your mind, because of your forbidding their worship and your disparaging of them. He said: "I call Allah to witness, and bear witness yourselves," that is, you too, "that I am free from what you associate with Him besides Him" (in one copy "tadhunna", which is an error). He means: I am free from all rivals and idols. "Then scheme against me all together," that is, you and your gods, if they are real, "and give me no respite," that is, not even for the blink of an eye.

* *

And His saying: "Indeed I have put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed my Lord is on a straight path" means: it is under His subjugation and authority, and He is the Just Judge who does not wrong in His judgment, for He is upon a straight path (sirat mustaqim).

Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Ayfa' ibn 'Abd al-Kala'i (ʿAbd al-Kalāʿī) that he said concerning the saying of the Exalted: "There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed my Lord is on a straight path," he said: "He takes hold of the forelocks of His servants. He meets the believer such that He is more compassionate to him than a father to his child, and it is said to the disbeliever: 'What has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord?' (82:6)."

This context contains a decisive argument and a conclusive proof of the truth of what he brought them, and of the falsehood of what they are upon of worshipping idols, which neither benefit nor harm, but are inert objects that neither hear nor see, neither befriend nor oppose. Sincere worship is due only to Allah alone, without partner, who holds the dominion in His hand, has absolute disposition, and over whom nothing is outside His dominion, power and authority. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

Say Hud to them [their messenger]: "If you turn away, I have already conveyed to you what I was sent with, namely the worship of Allah, your Lord, alone, without any partner. The proof has been established against you by my delivering to you the message of Allah with which He sent me. And ﴿My Lord will bring in a people other than you﴾ who will worship Him alone and not associate anything with Him, and He does not care for you. You will not harm Him by your disbelief; rather, the consequence of that will return upon you. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things﴾, that is, Witness and Keeper of the words and deeds of His servants, and He will recompense them for them: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil."

﴿And when Our command came﴾, which was the barren wind that Allah sent upon them, which did not pass over anything without reducing it to dust, Allah destroyed them completely, and He saved Hud, their messenger, and those who believed with him, from a severe punishment, by His mercy and kindness, the Exalted.

﴿And that was ʿAd; they denied the signs of their Lord﴾, that is, they disbelieved in them and disobeyed the messengers of Allah. This is because whoever disbelieves in one prophet has disbelieved in all the prophets, since there is no distinction among them in the obligation to believe in them. ʿAd disbelieved in Hud, so their disbelief was regarded as the disbelief of one who rejects all the messengers. ﴿And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾: they abandoned following their rightly guided messenger and followed the command of every obstinate tyrant. Therefore they were followed in this world by a curse from Allah and from His believing servants, whenever they are mentioned, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be proclaimed before the witnesses (on the heads of the assembled creation). ﴿Indeed, ʿAd disbelieved in their Lord. Ah, away with ʿAd, the people of Hud.﴾

Al-Suddi said: No prophet was sent after ʿAd except that they were cursed upon his tongue.

Therefore He said: "He produced you from the earth" (11:61), meaning He began your creation from it, from the earth from which He created your father Adam. "And He made you inhabit it" (11:61), meaning He made you settlers in it, who build it up and make it prosper and benefit from it, for your past sins. "Then turn to Him in repentance" (11:61), concerning what you will face in the future. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Ibrahim with the good tidings﴾, and they were the angels. It is said that the tidings were of Ishaq (Isaac), and it is said that they were of the destruction of the people of Lut (Lot). The first view is supported by His saying: ﴿So when the fear had left Ibrahim and the good tidings had reached him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lut﴾ [Hud: 74]. ﴿They said, "Peace." He said, "Peace"﴾, meaning: upon you.

The scholars of rhetoric (ʿulamaʾ al-bayan) said: this is better than how they greeted him, because the nominative (al-raf') indicates permanence and continuity.

﴿Then he did not delay but brought a roasted calf﴾, meaning: he went quickly and brought them hospitality. The calf (ʿijl) is a young cow, and ḥanidh is that which is roasted (mashwiyy), cooked thoroughly on hot stones (al-radf), which are heated stones.

This is the meaning reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and others, as He said in another verse: ﴿Then he turned quickly to his family and brought a fattened calf and set it before them. He said, "Will you not eat?"﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 26–27].

This verse contains many aspects of the etiquette of hospitality.

* *

His saying: ﴿But when he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he regarded them with suspicion﴾, meaning: he considered them strange, ﴿and he felt fear of them﴾. That is because the angels have no desire for food, do not crave it, and do not eat it. Therefore he saw their state as turning away from what he had brought them, entirely disinterested in it, and at that he regarded them with suspicion, and ﴿he felt fear of them﴾.

As-Suddi said: When Allah sent the angels to the people of Lut, they came walking in the form of young men, until they descended upon Ibrahim and he hosted them. When Ibrahim saw them, he honored them, ﴿and he went quickly to his family and brought a fattened calf﴾, slaughtered it, then roasted it on hot stones, and that is the ḥanidh when he roasted it. He brought it to them and sat with them, while Sarah stood serving them. This is when He says: "and his wife was standing while he was seated." In the reading of Ibn Masʿud: "So when he set it before them he said, 'Will you not eat?' They said, 'O Ibrahim, we do not eat food except for a price.' He said, 'Indeed for this there is a price.' They said, 'And what is its price?' He said, 'You mention the name of Allah over its first part and praise Him over its last.' Then Jibril looked at Mikail and said, 'It is right that this one should be taken by his Lord as a friend.'" ﴿When he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he regarded them with suspicion﴾ means: when he saw them not eating, he became frightened of them, and ﴿he felt fear of them﴾. When Sarah saw that he had honored them and she stood serving them, she laughed and said: "How strange are these guests of ours! We serve them ourselves out of honor for them, yet they do not eat our food."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Nasr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn Mihsan, concerning Ibrahim's guests, that he said: "They were four: Jibril, Mikail, Israfil, and Rafail." Nuh ibn Qays said: Nuh ibn Abi Shaddad claimed that when they entered upon Ibrahim and he brought the calf near them, Jibril wiped it with his wing, and it rose up running until it reached its mother, and the mother of the calf was in the house.

* *

His saying, reporting about the angels: ﴿They said, "Do not fear. Indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lut." And his wife was standing and she laughed﴾, meaning: they said, "Do not fear from us. We are angels sent to the people of Lut to destroy them." ﴿So she laughed﴾: Sarah laughed out of joy at their destruction, because of the abundance of their corruption and the severity of their disbelief and obstinacy. Therefore she was recompensed with the glad tidings of a son after despair.

Qatadah said: "His wife laughed and was amazed that a people whom punishment was coming to were in heedlessness, so she laughed at that and was amazed, and so We gave her the good tidings of Ishaq."

* *

His saying: ﴿And after Ishaq, Yaʿqub﴾. Al-ʿAwfi reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿she laughed﴾, meaning: she menstruated.

As for the view of Muhammad ibn Qays that she laughed because she thought they intended to act as the people of Lut acted, and the view of al-Kalbi that she laughed because of what she saw of Ibrahim's fear, both are very weak, and although Ibn Jarir narrated them with his chain to them, they should not be relied upon. And Allah knows best.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: she only laughed when she was given the good tidings of Ishaq. This contradicts this context, since the good tidings are explicitly stated as following from it.

﴿So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Yaʿqub﴾, meaning: a child for her who would have a child, offspring and descendants, for Yaʿqub was the son of Ishaq, as He said in the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Yaʿqub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim, Ismaʿil and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we are Muslims."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133].

From here, whoever argued from this verse that the one sacrificed was Ismaʿil, and that it is impossible that it was Ishaq, reasoned: the good tidings were given of him, and it was foretold that Yaʿqub would be born to him. How then would Ibrahim be commanded to slaughter him while he was a small child, and Yaʿqub, whose existence was promised, had not yet been born to him? And Allah's promise is true with no contradiction, so it is impossible that he be commanded to slaughter this one in such a state. Thus it is determined that it was Ismaʿil. This is among the finest, soundest and clearest arguments, and to Allah belongs all praise.

﴿She said, "Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this is my husband, an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing."﴾ He related her words in this verse, just as He related her action in the other verse, for she said: ﴿"Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman?"﴾, and in al-Dhariyat: ﴿So his wife came forward in a loud cry and struck her face and said, "An old barren woman!"﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 29], as is the custom of women in their words and actions when amazed. ﴿They said, "Are you amazed at the decree of Allah?"﴾, meaning: the angels said to her, "Do not be amazed at the decree of Allah, for when He wills a thing He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is. So do not be amazed at this, even if you are an old, barren woman, and your husband, the Khalil (friend) peace be upon him, is an elderly man, for indeed Allah is competent over all things."

﴿The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious﴾, meaning: He is the Praiseworthy in all His actions and statements, Glorified in His attributes and essence. For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs that they said: "We have known how to greet you, so how is the prayer upon you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.'" (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4797 and Sahih Muslim no. 406, from the hadith of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah, may Allah be pleased with him.)

* *

We will surely save him and his family, except his wife, who was among those who remained behind﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 32].

* *

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 11, verses 77–79:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the arrival of His messengers from among the angels, after they had informed Ibrahim (Abraham) of their mission and had parted from him, and had told him that Allah would destroy the people of Lut (Lot) that very night. So they set out from his presence and came to Lut, peace be upon him. He was, as has been said, in his land (which he cultivated), and it was also said that he was in his own house. They came to him in the most beautiful form, in the likeness of handsome young men, as a trial and a test from Allah, Whose is the wisdom and the conclusive proof. So they alighted with him, and his affairs grieved him and his soul was constricted on their account. He feared that if he did not host them, one of his people would host them and would harm them. ﴿He said, "This is a distressful day."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and other than one of the imams said: "Its trial is severe," because he knew that he would have to defend them against his people, and that this would be hard for him.

Qatadah mentioned that they came to him while he was in his land working in it, and they became his guests. He felt shy before them, so he walked ahead of them and said to them along the way, as one who hints to them that they should turn away from him: "By Allah, O people, I know of no people on the face of the earth more wicked than these." Then he walked a little and repeated that to them, until he had said it four times. Qatadah said: They had been commanded not to destroy them until their prophet had testified against them with that.

Al-Suddi said: The angels left Ibrahim heading toward the town of Lut. They reached the river of Sudun at midday, and they met the daughter of Lut drawing water for her family. Lut had two daughters: the elder was named Rathya and the younger Zaghurata. They said to her: "O girl, is there a place to stay?" She said to them: "Wait where you are until I come to you," and she fled from her people to them. Then she went to her father and said: "O my father, catch up with the young men at the gate of the city. I have never seen faces of people more beautiful than theirs. Your people will not take them and disgrace them." Now his people had forbidden him from hosting any man, and they had said: "Leave us alone, and let us host the men." So he brought them, and no one knew of them except the people of his household. Then his wife went out and told her people: "In the house of Lut there are men whose faces I have never seen the like of." So his people came rushing to him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿rushing toward him﴾, it means they hurried and ran in their walking, racing out of their joy at this.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And before that they had been doing evil deeds﴾, it means this had remained their habit until another time, until they were seized while in that state.

And His saying ﴿He said, "O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you"﴾ is him guiding them to their wives, for the prophet is to his community like a father to his children, both men and women. So he directed them to what is most beneficial for them in this world and the Hereafter, just as He said to them in another verse: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a people transgressing.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 165–166]. And His saying in another verse: ﴿They said, "Did we not forbid you from the worlds?"﴾ [al-Hijr: 70], meaning: "Did we not forbid you from hosting men?" ﴿He said, "These are my daughters, if you are going to act." By your life, indeed they were in their intoxication, wandering blindly.﴾ [al-Hijr: 71–72]. In this noble verse He says: ﴿These are my daughters; they are purer for you.﴾ Mujahid said: They were not his daughters in the literal sense, but they were from among his community, and every prophet is a father to his community.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Allah the Exalted informs about His Prophet Lut, peace be upon him: Lut warned them with his words: "﴿If only I had against you some power, or could take refuge in some strong support!﴾" That is, "I would surely have punished you and done to you the deeds (of punishment), with the torment and vengeance and the bringing of severe harm upon you, [by myself and my kin]."

For this reason there came in a hadith, by way of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Alqamah, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on Lut; he used to take refuge in a strong support," meaning Allah, Mighty and Majestic. "Allah did not send any prophet after him except that he was in a strong tribe of his people." (Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3116, by way of al-Fadl ibn Musa from Muhammad ibn Amr with the same wording. He also narrated it by way of Abdah and Abd al-Rahim from Muhammad ibn Amr, similar to the hadith of al-Fadl ibn Musa, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This second route is more authentic than the narration of al-Fadl ibn Musa, and this is a hasan hadith.")

It was also narrated as a marfu' report from the hadith of al-Zuhri from Abu Salamah and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab from Abu Hurayrah, and from the hadith of Abu al-Zinad from al-A'raj from Abu Hurayrah with the same wording, and from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah from Abu Yunus, who heard Abu Hurayrah with the same wording; and al-Hasan and Qatadah narrated it as a mursal report.

Then the angels informed him that they were the messengers of Allah sent to him, and gave him the good news that they could not reach him, [and without any harm]: ﴿They said, "O Lut, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you."﴾ They commanded him to travel with his family during the last part of the night, and to follow behind them, meaning he should be the rear guard of his family: ﴿And let none of you look back﴾, that is, when you hear what has befallen them, and let not those frightening sounds terrify you, but continue going on [just as you are].

Likewise Ibn Mas'ud read it, and put "your wife" in the accusative, because it is an exception from an affirmative sentence, so the accusative is required according to them.

So a stone came down upon her from the sky and killed her.

When Lut set out with them to his home, he remembered the evil deeds his people were committing, [and the great calamities], so he walked with them for a while, then turned to them and said, "Do you not know what the people of this town do? Then he walked with them for a while, and when he reached the middle of the town, and he pitied them and felt shame before them, he said, "Do you not know what the people of this town do? I know of no people on the face of the earth more evil than them; indeed my people are the worst of Allah's creation." Gabriel turned to the angels and said, "Remember; these are two." When he reached the door of the house, he wept out of shame before them and out of pity for them, and said, "Indeed my people are worse than Allah's creation? Do you not know what the people of this town do? I know of no people in the town on the face of the earth more evil than them." Gabriel said to the angels, "Remember; this is three. He stood in the form in which he is in heaven, spread his wing, and Gabriel has two wings; upon him was a sash of strung pearls, bright of teeth, clear of brow, his head had curly locks like coral, which is pearl, like snow, and his legs were greenish. Then he said, "O Lut, ﴿we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you.﴾ Step aside from the door, O Lut, and leave me with them." That is, He rained upon them stones of sijjil. It is said that sijjil in Persian means stones of clay, as reported by Ibn 'Abbas and others.

Some of them said: it means from sanak, which is stone, and gil, which is clay. In another verse He said: ﴿Stones of clay﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 51:33], meaning hardened, strong and firm. Some said: baked. Some said: cooked, strong and hard. Al-Bukhari said: "Sijjil: the strong and great." Sijjil and sijjin are one; the lam and the nun are sister letters. Tamim ibn Muqbil said:

"And a band who strike the helmets in the open field, a blow with which the champions have enjoined one another, sijjina."

[Sahih al-Bukhari (8/352), Fath al-Bari.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Layered﴾ (mandud), some said: layered in the sky, that is, prepared for this purpose.

Others said: ﴿Layered﴾ means that some of them follow others in their descent upon them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Marked﴾ (musawwama), it means marked, sealed, with the names of their owners upon them; every stone was inscribed with the name of the one on whom it would fall.

Qatadah and Ikrimah said: ﴿Marked﴾ means ringed, having a reddish sprinkling upon it.

They mention that it fell upon the people of the town and upon those scattered in the villages around it. While one of them was among the people, speaking, a stone would come down from the sky and fall upon him from among the people and destroy him. The stones followed them from all the lands until they destroyed them to the last one, and none of them remained.

Mujahid said: Jibril seized the people of Lot from their pastures and their homes, lifted them with their livestock and their belongings, and raised them until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs; then he overturned them. He said: they were carried on the outer part of his right wing. He said: when he overturned it, the first things to fall from it were its battlements.

Qatadah said: We have been told that Jibril took hold of the middle town by its handle, then swung it up toward the air of the sky, until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs; then he made some of it fall upon others, then he sent after the scattered people stones of sakhr (hard rock). He said: We have been told they were four towns, each with a hundred thousand people. In another narration: they were three towns, the greatest of which was Sodom. He said: We have been told that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to look out over Sodom and say: "Sodom, O day, what is the matter with you?"

In another narration from Qatadah and others: We have been told that when Jibril, peace be upon him, arose in the morning, he spread his wing, and uprooted their land with what was in it of palaces, animals, stones, trees, and everything in it. He gathered it into his wing, folded it and carried it within the hollow of his wing, then ascended with it to the lowest heaven, until the inhabitants of the heaven heard the voices of the people and the dogs, and they were four thousand thousand. Then he overturned it, sent it down to the earth upside down, and crushed some of it upon others, so He made its highest part its lowest, then sent stones of sijjil after it.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The towns of the people of Lot were five towns: Sodom, which was the greatest, and Sa'bah, Sa'wah, 'Ithrah, and Duma. Jibril carried them on his wing and ascended with them, so that the people of the lowest heaven heard the barking of their dogs and the crowing of their roosters; then he overturned them onto their faces, and Allah sent stones after them. Allah says: ﴿We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of sijjil﴾, so Allah destroyed it and what was around it of the overturned cities.

As-Suddi said: When the people of Lot awoke, Jibril descended, uprooted the earth from seven earths, carried it until he brought it up to the sky, until the people of the lowest heaven heard the barking of their dogs and the crowing of their roosters; then he overturned it and killed them. That is His saying: ﴿And the overturned city He hurled down﴾ [An-Najm 53:53]. And whoever did not die when it fell to the earth, Allah rained stones upon him while he was beneath the earth. And whoever of them was scattered in the land following them in the villages, a man would be speaking and a stone would come to him and kill him. That is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We rained upon them﴾, meaning in the villages, stones of sijjil. Thus said As-Suddi.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: this retribution is not far from whoever resembles them in their wrongdoing.

It has been transmitted in the hadith narrated in the Sunan, from the narration of Amr ibn Abi Amr from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, traced to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lot, kill the one who does it and the one it is done to." [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4462), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1456), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2561). al-Tirmidhi said: "This hadith is known only from Ibn 'Abbas from the Prophet ﷺ through this route. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this hadith from Amr ibn Abi Amr, saying: 'Cursed is whoever does the deed of the people of Lot,' and did not mention killing in it, and mentioned in it: 'Cursed is whoever has intercourse with an animal.'"]

Imam al-Shafi'i, in one of his opinions, and a group of scholars went to the view that the one who commits sodomy is to be killed, whether he is married or not married, acting upon this hadith.

Imam Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, went to the view that he is to be thrown from a high place and stones are to be pelted after him, as Allah did to the people of Lot. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best what is correct.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest﴾. This happened at sunrise. ﴿And We rained upon it stones of sijjil﴾ (the town was their great city, and it was Sodom [and its surroundings]), ﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest﴾, as in His saying: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down, and covered them with what covered﴾ [An-Najm 53:53-54]. That is, He rained upon them stones of sijjil. It is said that sijjil in Persian means stones of clay, as reported by Ibn 'Abbas and others.

Some of them said: it means from sanak, which is stone, and gil, which is clay. In another verse He said: ﴿Stones of clay﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 51:33], meaning hardened, strong and firm. Some said: baked. Some said: cooked, strong and hard. Al-Bukhari said: "Sijjil: the strong and great." Sijjil and sijjin are one; the lam and the nun are sister letters. Tamim ibn Muqbil said:

"And a band who strike the helmets in the open field, a blow with which the champions have enjoined one another, sijjina."

[Sahih al-Bukhari (8/352), Fath al-Bari.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Layered﴾ (mandud), some said: layered in the sky, that is, prepared for this purpose.

Others said: ﴿Layered﴾ means that some of them follow others in their descent upon them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Marked﴾ (musawwama), it means marked, sealed, with the names of their owners upon them; every stone was inscribed with the name of the one on whom it would fall.

Qatadah and Ikrimah said: ﴿Marked﴾ means ringed, having a reddish sprinkling upon it.

They mention that it fell upon the people of the town and upon those scattered in the villages around it. While one of them was among the people, speaking, a stone would come down from the sky and fall upon him from among the people and destroy him. The stones followed them from all the lands until they destroyed them to the last one, and none of them remained.

Mujahid said: Jibril seized the people of Lot from their pastures and their homes, lifted them with their livestock and their belongings, and raised them until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs; then he overturned them. He said: they were carried on the outer part of his right wing. He said: when he overturned it, the first things to fall from it were its battlements.

Qatadah said: We have been told that Jibril took hold of the middle town by its handle, then swung it up toward the air of the sky, until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs; then he made some of it fall upon others, then he sent after the scattered people stones of sakhr (hard rock). He said: We have been told they were four towns, each with a hundred thousand people. In another narration: they were three towns, the greatest of which was Sodom. He said: We have been told that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to look out over Sodom and say: "Sodom, O day, what is the matter with you?"

In another narration from Qatadah and others: We have been told that when Jibril, peace be upon him, arose in the morning, he spread his wing, and uprooted their land with what was in it of palaces, animals, stones, trees, and everything in it. He gathered it into his wing, folded it and carried it within the hollow of his wing, then ascended with it to the lowest heaven, until the inhabitants of the heaven heard the voices of the people and the dogs, and they were four thousand thousand. Then he overturned it, sent it down to the earth upside down, and crushed some of it upon others, so He made its highest part its lowest, then sent stones of sijjil after it.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The towns of the people of Lot were five towns: Sodom, which was the greatest, and Sa'bah, Sa'wah, 'Ithrah, and Duma. Jibril carried them on his wing and ascended with them, so that the people of the lowest heaven heard the barking of their dogs and the crowing of their roosters; then he overturned them onto their faces, and Allah sent stones after them. Allah says: ﴿We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of sijjil﴾, so Allah destroyed it and what was around it of the overturned cities.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this hadith from Amr ibn Abi Amr, saying: 'Cursed is whoever does the deed of the people of Lot,' and did not mention killing in it, and mentioned in it: 'Cursed is whoever has intercourse with an animal.'"]

Imam Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, went to the view that he is to be thrown from a high place and stones are to be pelted after him, as Allah did to the people of Lot. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best what is correct.

The Exalted says: And We sent to Madyan their brother Shu'ayb. They were a tribe of the Arabs, who dwelt between the Hijaz and the Levant, near the lands of Ma'an, in a town known after them, called "Madyan." So God sent to them Shu'ayb, who was among the most noble of them in lineage. Hence He said: ﴿their brother Shu'ayb﴾, who commanded them to worship God alone and forbade them from cheating (tatfif) in measure and weight. ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing day﴾. That is: in your livelihood and your provision, so I fear that you will be deprived of what you enjoy because of your violating the sanctities of God. ﴿And indeed I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing day﴾. That is: in the Hereafter.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 11, verses 85–86:

He first forbade them from cheating in measure and weight when they gave to people. Then he commanded them to give full measure and weight with justice, both when taking and when giving, and he forbade them from causing corruption on the earth (al-'ayth fi al-ard bi'l-fasad). They used to cut off the road.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿What remains with Allah is better for you﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: The provision of Allah is better for you.

Al-Hasan said: The provision of Allah is better for you than your defrauding people.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The commandment of Allah is better for you.

Mujahid said: Obedience to Allah is better for you.

Qatadah said: Your share from Allah is better for you.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Destruction" refers to the punishment, and "what remains" refers to mercy.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: ﴿What remains with Allah is better for you﴾ means: what remains of profit to you after giving full measure and weight is better for you, ﴿better for you﴾, that is, than taking the wealth of people. He said: This has also been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

I say: This resembles His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the evil impresses you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 100].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And I am not a watcher over you﴾, meaning: I am not a guardian or a keeper over you. That is, do that for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not do it so that people will see you, but for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 11, verses 85–86:

He first forbade them from cheating in measure and weight when they gave to people. Then he commanded them to give full measure and weight with justice, both when taking and when giving, and he forbade them from causing corruption on the earth (al-'ayth fi al-ard bi'l-fasad). They used to cut off the road.

Qatadah said: Your share from Allah is better for you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And I am not a watcher over you﴾, meaning: I am not a guardian or a keeper over you. That is, do that for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not do it so that people will see you, but for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

They say to him, in mockery, may Allah curse them: "Does your prayer (ﷺ) command you..." Al-A'mash said: "That is, your recitation (of the Qur'an)," ﴿Does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped﴾, i.e., the idols and statues, ﴿or that we should do with our wealth as we wish﴾, so that we would abandon giving less in measure (al-tatfif) at your word. Our wealth is ours; we do with it what we want.

[Al-Hasan said] regarding His words, ﴿Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped﴾: "By Allah, indeed his prayer does command them to abandon what their fathers used to worship."

Al-Thawri said regarding His words, ﴿or that we should do with our wealth as we wish﴾: "They mean the zakah."

* *

As for their words, ﴿Indeed you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾, Ibn 'Abbas, Maymun ibn Mihran, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Aslam and Ibn Jarir said: "The enemies of Allah say that in mockery. May Allah curse them and banish them from His mercy, and He has indeed done so."

He says to them: "Tell me, O my people, ﴿if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾," meaning, upon insight into what I call you to, ﴿and He has given me good provision from Himself﴾. It was said: he meant prophethood. It was also said: he meant lawful provision, and the phrase may include both meanings.

Al-Thawri said: ﴿Nor do I intend to oppose you in what I forbid you﴾, meaning: I do not forbid you from something and then secretly do it, hiding it from you.[[في ت، أ: "الشيء".]] This is like what Qatadah said regarding His words: ﴿Nor do I intend to oppose you in what I forbid you﴾, he said: "I would not forbid you from a matter and then commit it myself."[[في أ: "وأرتكبه".]] ﴿I intend only reform as far as I am able﴾, meaning: in what I command you and forbid you. My only aim is your reform, to the best of my effort and capacity. ﴿And my success is only through Allah﴾, meaning: in reaching the truth in what I intend. ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾, in all my affairs, ﴿and to Him I turn back in repentance﴾, meaning: I return. This was said by Mujahid and others.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Abu Qaza'ah Suwayd ibn Hujayr al-Bahili narrated to us, from Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah, from his father, that his brother Malik said: "O Mu'awiyah, Muhammad has seized my neighbours. Go to him, for he has spoken with you and knows you." So I went with him, and he said: "Leave my neighbours to me, for they had embraced Islam." He turned away from him, and [he got up, sulking][[زيادة من ت، أ، والمسند.،]] and said: "By Allah, if you do this, people will claim that you order a matter and then oppose it by doing something else." I kept dragging him while he spoke. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is he saying?" He said: "By Allah, if you do that, people will indeed claim that you order a matter and then oppose it by doing something else." He said: "Have they said this, or has one of them said it? And if I did that, the blame would fall upon me alone, and they bear no part of it. Release his neighbours to him."[[المسند (٤/٤٤٧) .]]

Ahmad also said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Bahz[[في ت، أ: "شهر".]] ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ seized some people from my folk on a charge, and detained them. A man from my folk came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was delivering a sermon and said: 'O Muhammad, on what grounds are you detaining my neighbours?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell silent [regarding him][[زيادة من ت، أ، والمسند.]], and he said: 'People are saying that you forbid a thing and then do it secretly.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'What is he saying?' I began to phrase the words between them, fearing that he would hear them and invoke against my people a curse after which they would never prosper. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept at him until he understood it, and then he said: 'Have they said this, or has one of them said it? By Allah, if I did it, the blame would be upon me and not upon them. Release his neighbours to him.'"[[المسند (٥/٢) ورواه أبو داود في السنن برقم (٣٦٣٠) عن عبد الرزاق والترمذي في السنن برقم (١٤١٧) عن ابن المبارك كلاهما من طريق معمر به مختصرا جدا، وقال الترمذي: "حديث بهز عن أبيه عن جده حديث حسن".]]

Of this kind is also the hadith that Imam Ahmad narrated: Abu Amir narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, who said: "I heard Abu Humayd and Abu Usayd saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'When you hear a hadith from me that your hearts recognise, and your hair and skins soften towards it, and you feel that it is close to you, then I am the closest of you to it. And when you hear a hadith from me that your hearts reject, and your hair and skins recoil from it, and you feel that it is far from you, then I am the farthest of you from it.'"[[المسند (٣/٤٩٧) .]]

This is a sound chain (isnad). Muslim has also transmitted through this same chain the hadith: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him say: 'O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy,' and when he leaves, let him say: 'O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.'"[[صحيح مسلم برقم (٧١٣) .]]

Its meaning, and Allah knows best: whatever good reaches you from me, I am the closest of you to it, and whatever is disliked, I am the farthest of you from it. ﴿Nor do I intend to oppose you in what I forbid [you][[زيادة من ت، أ.]]﴾.

Qatadah said, from Azrah[[في ت، أ: "عروة".]], from al-Hasan al-Urani, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from Masruq, that a woman came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "Do you forbid the wasilah?" He said: "Yes." She said: "[The woman][[زيادة من ت، أ.]] then perhaps it is in some of your wives?" He said: "Then I would not have memorised the counsel of the righteous servant: ﴿Nor do I intend to oppose you in what I forbid you﴾."

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah said: Jarir narrated to us, from Abu Sulayman al-Utbi[[في ت، أ: "الضبي".]], who said: "The letters of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz used to reach us containing commands and prohibitions, and at the end of them he would write: 'And I have not been in any of this except as the righteous servant said: ﴿And my success is only through Allah; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back in repentance﴾.'"

He says to them: "And O my people, let not my opposition (shiqaq) bring upon you [the like of] what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih, and the people of Lut in terms of punishment and chastisement." That is, let not my enmity and hostility toward you lead you to persist in the disbelief and corruption you are upon, so that there befalls you the like of what befell the people of Noah, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, and the people of Lut.

Qatadah said: "[Let not] my opposition [shiqaqi] bring you to ruin" means: let not my separation from you (firaqi) lead you [to it].

As-Suddi said: "[My opposition]" means my enmity, so that you persist in misguidance and disbelief, and there befalls you the punishment that befell them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to us, Abu al-Mughirah Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Ibn Abi Ghaniyyah narrated to us, Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman narrated to me, from Abu Layla al-Kindi, who said: I was with my master, holding his mount, while the people had surrounded Uthman ibn Affan. Then he looked down upon us from his house and said: "And O my people, let not my opposition bring upon you [the like of] what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih." O my people, do not kill me; for if you kill me, you will be [divided] like this, and he interlaced his fingers.

* *

They said: "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say," meaning: we neither comprehend nor grasp much of your speech. "And there is deafness in our ears, and between us and you there is a barrier." "And indeed, we see you as weak among us."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Thawri said: he was blind in sight. Al-Thawri said: he was called "the orator of the prophets" (khatib al-anbiya').

[And al-Suddi said regarding "And indeed, we see you as weak among us": "You are alone."]

[And Abu Rawq said regarding "And indeed, we see you as weak among us," meaning: humiliated, because your tribe is not upon your religion, so you are humiliated and weak.]

It was said: "stoned" with stones; and it was said: "we would have cursed you." "And you are not mighty against us," meaning: you have no standing with us.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 11, verse 93–95:

When the Prophet of Allah, Shu'ayb, despaired of his people responding to him, he said: "O my people, ﴿work according to your station﴾, that is, according to your way. This is a severe threat and warning. ﴿Indeed, I am working﴾ according to my way and my method. ﴿You will soon know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him﴾, that is, in the Hereafter, ﴿and who is a liar﴾, that is, whether it is I or you. ﴿And wait﴾, that is, await, ﴿indeed I am with you, a watcher.﴾"

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the cry seized those who had wronged, so they became within their homes prostrate, lifeless.﴾ Those who wronged were his people. The word ﴿prostrate﴾ means: motionless, without any movement in them. Here it is mentioned that a cry (sayha) came upon them, while in al-A'raf it is mentioned as an earthquake (rajfa), and in al-Shu'ara' it is mentioned as the punishment of the Day of the Canopy (yawm al-zulla). They were one nation, and on the day of their punishment all these calamities gathered upon them. God, exalted is He, says, informing about the sending of Musa (peace be upon him) with His signs, clear proofs, decisive arguments and manifest evidences, to Fir'awn (Pharaoh), may Allah curse him, who was the king of the lands of Egypt over the nation of the Copts. ﴿But they followed the command of Pharaoh﴾, that is, his course, his method and his way of misguidance and error. ﴿And the command of Pharaoh was not right-guiding﴾, that is, there was in it no right guidance nor any guidance; rather it was ignorance, misguidance, disbelief and obstinacy. Just as they followed him in this world, and he was their leader and chief, so too he will lead them on the Day of Resurrection into the Fire of Hell, and he will bring them into it, and they will drink from the watering-places of its destruction. He will have in that the greatest share of the greatest punishment, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, and We seized him with a severe seizing﴾ [al-Muzzammil 73:16]. And God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So he denied and disobeyed. Then he turned away, striving. And he gathered [his people] and proclaimed, saying, "I am your lord, the most high." So Allah seized him in the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life]. Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears [Allah]﴾ [an-Nazi'at 79:21–26]. And God, exalted is He, said: ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are led﴾. And such is the condition of those who are followed: they will be given a multiplied share of punishment on the Day of Return, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿[He] said, "For each there is double [punishment], but you do not know"﴾ [al-A'raf 7:38]. And God, exalted is He, reported about the disbelievers that they will say in the Fire: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they misguided us from the way. Our Lord, give them double punishment from the Fire and curse them with a great curse﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:67–68].

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, Abu al-Jahm narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Imru' al-Qays, the bearer of the banner of the poets of the Jahiliyyah, [is going] to the Fire."
[Al-Musnad (2/228).]

Mujahid, Qatadah and others said: meaning, nothing but loss (takhsir). That is because the cause of their destruction and ruin was only their following those gods and worshipping them. Thus what befell them befell them, and they lost by means of them, in this world and the Hereafter.

Allah says: "Just as We destroyed those earlier generations who were wrongdoers and denied Our messengers, so We do with their likes, their counterparts and their kind": ﴿Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.﴾

In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4686), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2583).]]

And as evidence for the truth of Our promise concerning the Hereafter, [Allah says]: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand.﴾ [Ghafir: 51]. Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿So their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers and will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears My standing [before Me] and fears My threat."﴾ [Ibrahim: 13, 14].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is a Day on which mankind will be assembled﴾ [[Before it, in manuscripts T and A: "Indeed in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter."]] meaning: the first of them and the last of them, so that not one of them is left behind, as He said: ﴿And We gathered them and left out none of them﴾ [Al-Kahf: 47].

﴿And that is a Day witnessed﴾ meaning: a great Day attended by all the angels, on which all the messengers gather, and all creation is gathered together, from mankind, jinn, birds, wild animals and beasts, and the Just One judges among them, who does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it.

As for His statement: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a term already counted﴾, meaning: We do not delay the establishment of the Day of Resurrection except because the word of Allah, His decree and His predestination, has preceded concerning the existence of a counted number of people from the descendants of Adam. He has set a specific term, and when it expires and the existence of those whose emergence from the descendants of Adam was decreed is completed, Allah will establish the Hour. For this reason He said: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a term already counted﴾, meaning: for a fixed period that is neither increased nor decreased. ﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission﴾. He says: on the Day this Day comes, which is the Day of Resurrection, no one will speak except by the permission of Allah the Exalted, as He said: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows, none will speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct﴾ [An-Naba': 38]. And He said: ﴿And voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾ [Ta-Ha: 108]. In the Two Sahihs [Bukhari and Muslim], from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the lengthy hadith of intercession: "No one will speak on that Day except the messengers, and the supplication of the messengers on that Day will be: O Allah, grant safety, grant safety." [[In T: "O Allah, grant safety, O Allah, grant safety."]] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (806), and Sahih Muslim, no. (182).]]

Then Allah the Exalted explained the condition of the wretched and the condition of the happy, saying:

And as evidence for the truth of Our promise concerning the Hereafter, [Allah says]: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand.﴾ [Ghafir: 51]. Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿So their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers and will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears My standing [before Me] and fears My threat."﴾ [Ibrahim: 13, 14].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is a Day on which mankind will be assembled﴾ [[Before it, in manuscripts T and A: "Indeed in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter."]] meaning: the first of them and the last of them, so that not one of them is left behind, as He said: ﴿And We gathered them and left out none of them﴾ [Al-Kahf: 47].

﴿And that is a Day witnessed﴾ meaning: a great Day attended by all the angels, on which all the messengers gather, and all creation is gathered together, from mankind, jinn, birds, wild animals and beasts, and the Just One judges among them, who does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿For them therein will be groaning and wailing.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "The zafir (groaning) is in the throat, and the shahiq (wailing) is in the chest. That is, their exhaling is zafir, and their inhaling is shahiq, because of the punishment they are in. We seek refuge with Allah from that."

﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure.﴾ The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: "It is a habit of the Arabs, when they want to describe something as lasting forever, to say: 'This is lasting as long as the heavens and the earth endure.' They also say: 'It remains as long as night and day alternate, as long as the two sons of Samir keep talking by night, and as long as the gazelles (al-'ufr) flick their tails.' They mean by this the word 'forever' (abadan). So Allah, may His praise be exalted, addressed them with what they know among themselves, saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure.﴾"

I (Ibn Kathir) say: It is also possible that what is meant by "as long as the heavens and the earth endure" is the kind (of heavens and earth), because in the world of the Hereafter there must be heavens and an earth, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the day the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens [as well]﴾ [Ibrahim: 48]. For this reason al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding His words ﴿as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: "A heaven other than this heaven will be substituted, and an earth other than this earth, so long as that heaven and that earth endure."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was related from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: "For every Paradise there is a heaven and an earth."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "As long as the earth is earth and the heaven is heaven."

* *

As for His words ﴿except what your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is the Effector of what He intends﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except what Allah wills. Indeed your Lord is Wise, Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 128].

The commentators have differed regarding the meaning of this exception, with many opinions, which Shaykh Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi related in his book "Zad al-Masir" [[Zad al-Masir (4/160, 161).]] and other scholars of tafsir. Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, transmitted many of them in his book [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/485).]], and he chose what he transmitted from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Abu Sinan. Ibn Abi Hatim also related from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan: that the exception refers to the sinners among the people of monotheism (tawhid), whom Allah will bring out of the Fire through the intercession of those who intercede, from among the angels, the prophets and the believers, when they intercede for the people of major sins. Then the mercy of the Most Merciful of the Merciful will come, and it will bring out from the Fire the one who has never done a single good deed and who once said: "There is no god but Allah." This is what the authentic and widely transmitted reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicate, with the same meaning, from the hadith of Anas, Jabir, Abu Sa'id, Abu Hurayrah and others among the Companions [[See the hadiths of intercession under the tafsir of Surah al-Isra' at its beginning.]]. After that, none will remain in the Fire except those for whom eternal abiding in it has been decreed and for whom there is no escape from it. This is the view held by many scholars, past and present, in the interpretation of this noble verse.

It has also been related in its interpretation from the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayrah, 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, Jabir and Abu Sa'id, among the Companions; and from Abu Mijlaz, al-Sha'bi and others among the Successors; and from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and others among the imams, strange opinions. A strange hadith has also come in al-Tabarani's "al-Mu'jam al-Kabir", from Abu Umamah Sudayy ibn 'Ajlan al-Bahili, but its chain is weak. And Allah knows best.

Qatadah said: "Allah knows best its meaning (thunya'uhu)."

Al-Suddi said: "It is abrogated (mansukhah) by His saying: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Nisa': 57]."
