﴿And as for those who were made happy﴾, they are the followers of the messengers, ﴿they will be in the Garden﴾, meaning their abode is the Garden, ﴿abiding therein﴾, meaning remaining and dwelling therein forever, ﴿for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾. The meaning of the exception here is that their enduring in the bliss they are in is not something necessary in itself. Rather, it is left to the will of Allah, the Exalted, so the favor is His upon them [always] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]]. For this reason they are inspired to glorify and praise (Allah) just as they are inspired to breathe.

Al-Dahhak and al-Hasan al-Basri said: it refers to the monotheists who were disobedient and who were in the Fire, and then were brought out of it. He followed this with His saying: ﴿a gift that is never cut off﴾, meaning not severed [[In manuscript A: "cut off."]]. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah and others, so that no one would suppose, after the mention of the exception, that there is any cessation, or ambiguity, or anything of the sort. Rather, He concluded it with permanence and the absence of cessation. Likewise, He clarified there that the punishment of the people of the Fire in the Fire is eternal, subject to His will, and that He punished them by His justice and wisdom. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Doer of what He wills﴾ [Hud: 107], just as He said: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya: 23]. Here He comforted the hearts and confirmed the intended meaning by His saying: ﴿a gift that is never cut off﴾.

"O people of Paradise, there is eternal life with no death. O people of the Fire, there is eternal life with no death" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4730, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2849, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him].

And in the two Sahihs also: "It will be said: O people of Paradise, indeed for you is that you will live and never die; and indeed for you is that you will be young and never grow old; and indeed for you is that you will be healthy and never fall ill; and indeed for you is that you will enjoy bliss and never be miserable" [Sahih Muslim, no. 2837, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them both. I did not find it in al-Bukhari.] [[In manuscript A: "In the Sahih."]] [[In manuscripts T and A: "Then it is said" / "said" variant.]]

Allah says: ﴿So do not be in doubt about what these [polytheists] worship.﴾ It is falsehood, ignorance and misguidance, for they only worship what their fathers worshipped before them. That is, they have no basis for what they are upon except following their fathers in ignorance. Allah will repay them for that in full: He will punish their disbelievers with a punishment that He inflicts on no one else among the worlds. And if they have any good deeds, Allah has already paid them for them in this world before the Hereafter.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And indeed, We will pay them their portion without reduction﴾ that he said: "[It is] what they were promised of good or evil."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "﴿Indeed, We will pay them their portion of the punishment without reduction.﴾"

Then He mentioned that He gave Musa the Book, and people differed about it: some believed in it and some disbelieved in it. So, O Muhammad, there is an example for you in the prophets who came before you, so let their denial of you not anger you, and let it not weigh heavily upon you.

﴿And were it not for a word that had preceded from your Lord, the matter would have been decided between them.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: Were it not for what preceded of His deferring the punishment to a specified term, Allah would have decided between them.

It is also possible that the meaning of "the word" is that He does not punish anyone except after the establishment of proof against him and the sending of a messenger to him, as He said: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra' 15]. For He said in another verse: ﴿And were it not for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term [would have been fixed]. So be patient over what they say﴾ [Ta-Ha 129–130].

Then He informed that the disbelievers are in a doubt about what the Messenger brought them, a strong and disquieting doubt, so He said: ﴿And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt concerning it.﴾

Then He informed us that He will gather the first and the last of the nations and repay them for their deeds: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil. So He said: ﴿And indeed, to each your Lord will fully repay [their] deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.﴾ That is, He is Knowing of all their deeds, the great and the trivial, the small and the large.

There are many readings of this verse, and their meanings return to what we have mentioned, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed, all of them will be brought before Us [for judgment]﴾ [Ya-Sin 32].

Almighty Allah commands His Messenger and the believing servants to be steadfast and to persevere in uprightness, and this is among the greatest aids to victory over the enemies and to opposing the adversaries. He forbade transgression (ṭughyān), which is oppression (al-baghy), for it is a cause of ruin, even if it is directed at a polytheist. Allah also informed that He is All-Seeing of the deeds of His servants; He is not heedless of anything, and nothing is hidden from Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have wronged﴾, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "Do not be lax (lā tudhinū)." Al-ʿAwfī related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "It is inclining toward polytheism."

Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: "Do not be pleased with their deeds."

Ibn Jurayj related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "Do not lean toward those who have wronged." This statement is good, meaning: do not seek help from the wrongdoers, lest you appear as though you are content with the remainder of their conduct. ﴿Lest the Fire touch you, and you have no protectors other than Allah; then you will not be helped﴾, meaning: there is no protector besides Him who can rescue you, nor any helper who can deliver you from His punishment.

Ibn Jurayj related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "Do not lean toward those who have wronged." This statement is good, meaning: do not seek help from the wrongdoers, lest you appear as though you are content with the remainder of their conduct. ﴿Lest the Fire touch you, and you have no protectors other than Allah; then you will not be helped﴾, meaning: there is no protector besides Him who can rescue you, nor any helper who can deliver you from His punishment.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 11, verses 114–115 (part 1 of 2):

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾: he said, "It means the dawn (Ṣubḥ) prayer and the sunset (Maghrib) prayer." This was also the view of al-Ḥasan and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Al-Ḥasan, in one narration, along with Qatādah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others, said: "They are the dawn prayer and the afternoon (ʿAṣr) prayer."

Mujāhid said: "They are the dawn prayer at the beginning of the day, and the noon (Ẓuhr) and afternoon prayers at its end." Likewise said Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurẓī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk in one narration from him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and at the approaches of the night﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan and others said: "It means the night (ʿIshāʾ) prayer."

Al-Ḥasan, in a narration of Ibn al-Mubārak from Mubārak ibn Faḍālah from him, said: "It means the sunset and the night prayers." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the two approaches of the night: the sunset and the night prayers." [Narrated by al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsir (15/508).] Likewise said Mujāhid, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, Qatādah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk: they are the sunset and night prayers.

It is possible that this verse was revealed before the five prayers were made obligatory on the night of the Isrāʾ (Night Journey), for at that time only two prayers were obligatory: a prayer before the sunrise and a prayer before its setting. And during part of the night there was a night vigil (qiyām) obligatory upon him and upon the Ummah; then it was abrogated (naskh, i.e., cancelled by a later ruling) for the Ummah, while its obligation remained upon him, and then it was also abrogated for him, according to one opinion. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾: it means that doing good deeds expiates past sins, as came in the hadith narrated by Imām Aḥmad and the authors of the Sunan from the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: "When I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah benefited me with it as much as He willed. And when anyone related it to me, I made him swear, and when he swore to me, I believed him. Abū Bakr related to me, and Abū Bakr spoke truthfully, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'No Muslim commits a sin, then performs ablution and prays two rakʿahs, except that he is forgiven.'" [Musnad (1/2); Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (1521); Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (406); al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā no. (10247); Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1395). al-Tirmidhī said: "The hadith of ʿAlī is ḥasan (good), and we do not know it except from this route."]

And in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (Bukhārī and Muslim) from the Commander of the Faithful ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān: that he performed ablution for them in the same way as the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah perform ablution like this," and he said: "Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rakʿahs without letting his mind wander in them, will be forgiven his previous sins." [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. (159); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (245).]

Aḥmad and Abū Jaʿfar Ibn Jarīr narrated, from the hadith of Abū ʿAqīl Zuhrah ibn Maʿbad, that he heard al-Ḥārith, the client (mawlā) of ʿUthmān, say: "ʿUthmān sat one day and we sat with him. The muezzin came to him, so ʿUthmān asked for water in a vessel, which I think would have contained about a mudd (a measure), and he performed ablution. Then he said: 'I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) perform ablution like this ablution of mine.' Then he said: 'Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then stands and prays the Ẓuhr prayer, will be forgiven what is between it and the dawn prayer; then he prays the ʿAṣr prayer, and will be forgiven what is between it and the Ẓuhr prayer; then he prays the Maghrib prayer, and will be forgiven what is between it and the ʿAṣr prayer; then he prays the ʿIshāʾ prayer, and will be forgiven what is between it and the Maghrib prayer; then perhaps he sleeps, tossing and turning through the night; then if he gets up, performs ablution and prays the dawn prayer, he will be forgiven what is between it and the ʿIshāʾ prayer. And these are the good deeds that remove the evil deeds.'" [Musnad (1/71); Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (15/511).]

In the Ṣaḥīḥ (Bukhārī and Muslim) from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Tell me, if there were a flowing river at the door of one of you, in which he bathed five times every day, would any of his dirt remain?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Likewise are the five prayers; Allah erases by them sins and wrongdoings." [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. (528); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (667).]

Muslim said in his Ṣaḥīḥ: Abū al-Ṭāhir and Hārūn ibn Saʿīd related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, from Abū Ṣakhr, that ʿUmar ibn Isḥāq, the client of Zāʾidah, related to him from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramaḍān to Ramaḍān, are expiations for what is between them, provided the major sins are avoided." [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (233).]

Imām Aḥmad said: al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ related to us, Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿah, from Surayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, that Abū Ruhm al-Samʿī used to narrate that Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī related to him that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Indeed every prayer removes the sin that is before it." [Musnad (5/413).]

Abū Jaʿfar Ibn Jarīr said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf related to us, Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl related to us, my father related to us, from Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿah, from Surayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prayers have been made expiations for what is between them, for Allah said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾." [Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (15/513); Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl is weak and did not hear from his father.]

Al-Bukhārī said: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd related to us, Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ related to us, from Sulaymān al-Taymī, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from Ibn Masʿūd, that a man had kissed a woman, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and Allah revealed: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds.﴾ The man said: "Is this for me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "It is for all of my Ummah, every one of them." [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. (526) and no. (4687).]

Thus he narrated it in the Book of Prayer, and he related it in the Book of Tafsir from Musaddad, from Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ, with similar wording. Muslim, Aḥmad and the authors of the Sunan, except Abū Dāwūd, related it through several routes from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, whose name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mull. [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (2763); Musnad (1/385); Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (3114); al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā no. (11247); Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1398).]

Aḥmad, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Jarīr narrated, and this is his wording, through several routes from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, that he heard Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd narrate from ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I found a woman in an orchard, and I did everything with her except that I did not have intercourse with her. I kissed her and embraced her, and I did nothing beyond that. So do to me whatever you will." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said nothing, and the man left. ʿUmar said: "Allah has concealed him; if only he had concealed himself." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent after him with his gaze, then said: "Bring him back to me." They brought him back, and he recited to him: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ Muʿādh said, and in the narration of ʿUmar: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for him alone, or for all people?" He said: "Rather, it is for all people." [Musnad (1/445); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (2763); Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (4468); Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (3112); al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā no. (7323); Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (15/515).]

Aḥmad said: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd related to us, Abān ibn Isḥāq related to us, from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Muḥammad, from Murrah al-Hamdānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has distributed your characters among you as He distributed your provisions among you. Allah gives the world to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, but He does not give the religion except to whomever He loves. So whoever Allah gives the religion has indeed loved him. By Him in whose hand is my soul, a servant does not submit until his heart and tongue submit, and he does not believe until his neighbour is safe from his evils." We said: "And what are his evils, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "His cheating and his oppression. A servant does not earn unlawful wealth and then spend from it, and be blessed in it, nor give charity from it and have it accepted, nor leave it behind his back except that it becomes his provision to the Fire. Indeed Allah does not erase an evil with an evil, but He erases an evil with a good. Indeed, the wicked does not erase the wicked." [Musnad (1/387).]

Ibn Jarīr said: Abū al-Sāʾib related to us, Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "So-and-so ibn Muʿattib was a man from the Anṣār, and he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I entered upon a woman and I did with her what a man does with his wife, except that I did not have intercourse with her.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not know how to answer him until this verse was revealed: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called him and recited it to him." [Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (15/519).]

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he was ʿAmr ibn Ghaziyyah al-Anṣārī, the date seller. Muqātil said: he was Abū Nufayl ʿĀmir ibn Qays al-Anṣārī. Al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī mentioned that he was Abū al-Yasar Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr.

Imām Aḥmad said: Yūnus and ʿAffān related to us, both saying: Ḥammād, that is Ibn Salamah, related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd. ʿAffān said: ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to ʿUmar and said: "A woman came to buy from me, so I brought her into the storeroom, and I touched her with what is less than intercourse." ʿUmar said: "Woe to you! Perhaps she was a woman whose husband is away in the way of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Go to Abū Bakr and ask him." He went to him and asked him, and he said: "Perhaps she is a woman whose husband is away in the way of Allah?" and he said the same as ʿUmar. Then he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to him the same thing, and he said: "Perhaps she is a woman whose husband is away in the way of Allah." Then the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ until the end of the verse. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for me alone, or for all people?" ʿUmar struck his chest with his hand and said: "No, and not even the coolness of the eye [i.e., no, not at all]; rather, it is for all people." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "ʿUmar has spoken the truth." [Musnad (1/245); ʿAlī ibn Zayd is weak.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 11, verses 114–115 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated through Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Uthman ibn Mawhib, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu al-Yasar Ka'b ibn 'Amr al-Ansari, who said: A woman came to me to buy dates from me for a dirham. I said: "In the house there are dates better and finer than these." So she entered, and I reached out to her and kissed her. I came to Umar and asked him, and he said: "Fear Allah, conceal yourself, and do not tell anyone." But I could not bear it, so I came to Abu Bakr and asked him, and he said: "Fear Allah, conceal yourself, and do not tell anyone." He said: I could not bear it, so I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him. He said: "Did you betray a man who is fighting in the way of Allah, regarding his family, with the like of this?" until I thought I was among the people of the Fire, and I wished that I had not embraced Islam at that hour. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lowered his head for a while, and Jibril descended and said: "Where is Abu al-Yasar?" I came, and he recited to me: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ up to ﴿a reminder for those who remember﴾. A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for him specifically, or for people in general?" He said: "For people in general" (Tafsir al-Tabari, 15/523).

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni said: Al-Husayn ibn Isma'il al-Mahamili narrated to us, Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that he was sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who had relations with a woman who was not lawful to him, and he did everything a man may do with his wife except intercourse?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Perform ablution well, then stand and pray." Mu'adh said: So Allah revealed this verse, meaning His saying: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night﴾. Mu'adh asked: "Is it for him specifically, or for the Muslims in general?" He said: "Rather, for the Muslims in general."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through several chains, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, with the same wording (Sunan al-Daraqutni, 1/134; Tafsir al-Tabari, 15/520–522). Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan, no. 3113, through Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr with the same wording, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This hadith does not have a connected isnad (chain). Abd Allah ibn Abi Layla did not hear from Mu'adh. Shu'bah narrated this hadith from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a mursal (a report where a Successor omits the Companion)."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah, that a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned a woman while he was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He asked his permission for a need, and he was permitted. He went to look for her but did not find her. The man then set out wanting to give the Prophet (ﷺ) the good news of rain, and he found the woman sitting by a pool. He pushed her in the chest and sat between her legs, and his member became like a tuft of hair (hudbah). He stood up regretful until he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what he had done. He said to him: "Ask forgiveness from your Lord, and pray four rak'ahs." He said: And he recited to him: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night﴾ to the end of the verse (Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq, 1/274).

Ibn Jarir said: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabwayh narrated to me, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me, Abd Allah ibn Salim narrated to me, from al-Zubaydi, from Salim ibn Amir, that he heard Abu Umamah say: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, enforce the legal punishment of Allah upon me" (he said it once or twice). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away from him. Then the prayer was called, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) finished the prayer, he said: "Where is this man who said: 'Enforce upon me the legal punishment of Allah?'" He said: "Here I am." He said: "Did you complete the ablution and pray with us just now?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are free from your sin as on the day your mother bore you. Do not return to it." And Allah revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ (Tafsir al-Tabari, 15/521). Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, no. 2765, through Shaddad ibn Abd Allah, from Abu Umamah, with similar wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Abu Uthman, who said: I was with Salman al-Farisi under a tree. He took a dry branch from it and shook it until a leaf fell off. Then he said: "O Abu Uthman, will you not ask me why I do this?" I said: "Why do you do it?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did this to me when I was with him under a tree. He took a dry branch from it and shook it until a leaf fell off, and he said: 'O Salman, will you not ask me why I do this?'" I said: "And why do you do it?" He said: "When a Muslim performs ablution and does it well, then prays the five prayers, his sins fall away just as this leaf falls." And he said: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ (Musnad Ahmad, 5/437).

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O Mu'adh, follow the evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and treat people with good character" (Musnad Ahmad, 5/228).

Imam Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fear Allah wherever you are, follow the evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and treat people with good character" (Musnad Ahmad, 5/153).

Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shamr ibn 'Atiyyah, from his shaykhs, from Abu Dharr, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "When you commit an evil deed, follow it with a good deed and it will erase it." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is 'There is no god but Allah' among the good deeds?" He said: "It is the best of good deeds" (Musnad Ahmad, 5/169).

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Hudhayl ibn Ibrahim al-Jummani narrated to us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri narrated to us, from the descendants of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from al-Zuhri, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No servant says: 'There is no god but Allah' at any hour of night or day, except that the sins written in his record are wiped away, until he is at ease with the like of them in good deeds" (Musnad Abi Ya'la, 6/204). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/82): "In its chain is Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri, who is abandoned (matruk)."

Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman is called al-Waqqasi. There is weakness in him.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Bishr ibn Adam and Zayd ibn Akhram both narrated to us, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Mastur ibn Abbad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have left behind no need or small need (without addressing it)." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then this will cover that" (Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3067, Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/83): "Its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)").

Only Mastur narrated this hadith through this route.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 11, verses 114–115 (part 1 of 2):

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾: he said, "It means the dawn (Ṣubḥ) prayer and the sunset (Maghrib) prayer." This was also the view of al-Ḥasan and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Al-Ḥasan, in one narration, along with Qatādah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others, said: "They are the dawn prayer and the afternoon (ʿAṣr) prayer."

Mujāhid said: "They are the dawn prayer at the beginning of the day, and the noon (Ẓuhr) and afternoon prayers at its end." Likewise said Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurẓī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk in one narration from him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and at the approaches of the night﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan and others said: "It means the night (ʿIshāʾ) prayer."

Al-Ḥasan, in a narration of Ibn al-Mubārak from Mubārak ibn Faḍālah from him, said: "It means the sunset and the night prayers." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the two approaches of the night: the sunset and the night prayers." [Narrated by al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsir (15/508).] Likewise said Mujāhid, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, Qatādah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk: they are the sunset and night prayers.

It is possible that this verse was revealed before the five prayers were made obligatory on the night of the Isrāʾ (Night Journey), for at that time only two prayers were obligatory: a prayer before the sunrise and a prayer before its setting. And during part of the night there was a night vigil (qiyām) obligatory upon him and upon the Ummah; then it was abrogated (naskh, i.e., cancelled by a later ruling) for the Ummah, while its obligation remained upon him, and then it was also abrogated for him, according to one opinion. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾: it means that doing good deeds expiates past sins, as came in the hadith narrated by Imām Aḥmad and the authors of the Sunan from the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: "When I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah benefited me with it as much as He willed. And when anyone related it to me, I made him swear, and when he swore to me, I believed him. Abū Bakr related to me, and Abū Bakr spoke truthfully, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'No Muslim commits a sin, then performs ablution and prays two rakʿahs, except that he is forgiven.'" [Musnad (1/2); Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (1521); Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (406); al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā no. (10247); Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1395). al-Tirmidhī said: "The hadith of ʿAlī is ḥasan (good), and we do not know it except from this route."]

And in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (Bukhārī and Muslim) from the Commander of the Faithful ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān: that he performed ablution for them in the same way as the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah perform ablution like this," and he said: "Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rakʿahs without letting his mind wander in them, will be forgiven his previous sins." [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. (159); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (245).]

Aḥmad and Abū Jaʿfar Ibn Jarīr narrated, from the hadith of Abū ʿAqīl Zuhrah ibn Maʿbad, that he heard al-Ḥārith, the client (mawlā) of ʿUthmān, say: "ʿUthmān sat one day and we sat with him. The muezzin came to him, so ʿUthmān asked for water in a vessel, which I think would have contained about a mudd (a measure), and he performed ablution. Then he said: 'I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) perform ablution like this ablution of mine.' Then he said: 'Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then stands and prays the Ẓuhr prayer, will be forgiven what is between it and the dawn prayer; then he prays the ʿAṣr prayer, and will be forgiven what is between it and the Ẓuhr prayer; then he prays the Maghrib prayer, and will be forgiven what is between it and the ʿAṣr prayer; then he prays the ʿIshāʾ prayer, and will be forgiven what is between it and the Maghrib prayer; then perhaps he sleeps, tossing and turning through the night; then if he gets up, performs ablution and prays the dawn prayer, he will be forgiven what is between it and the ʿIshāʾ prayer. And these are the good deeds that remove the evil deeds.'" [Musnad (1/71); Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (15/511).]

In the Ṣaḥīḥ (Bukhārī and Muslim) from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Tell me, if there were a flowing river at the door of one of you, in which he bathed five times every day, would any of his dirt remain?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Likewise are the five prayers; Allah erases by them sins and wrongdoings." [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. (528); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (667).]

Muslim said in his Ṣaḥīḥ: Abū al-Ṭāhir and Hārūn ibn Saʿīd related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, from Abū Ṣakhr, that ʿUmar ibn Isḥāq, the client of Zāʾidah, related to him from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramaḍān to Ramaḍān, are expiations for what is between them, provided the major sins are avoided." [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (233).]

Imām Aḥmad said: al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ related to us, Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿah, from Surayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, that Abū Ruhm al-Samʿī used to narrate that Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī related to him that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Indeed every prayer removes the sin that is before it." [Musnad (5/413).]

Abū Jaʿfar Ibn Jarīr said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf related to us, Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl related to us, my father related to us, from Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿah, from Surayḥ ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prayers have been made expiations for what is between them, for Allah said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾." [Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (15/513); Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl is weak and did not hear from his father.]

Al-Bukhārī said: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd related to us, Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ related to us, from Sulaymān al-Taymī, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from Ibn Masʿūd, that a man had kissed a woman, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and Allah revealed: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds.﴾ The man said: "Is this for me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "It is for all of my Ummah, every one of them." [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. (526) and no. (4687).]

Thus he narrated it in the Book of Prayer, and he related it in the Book of Tafsir from Musaddad, from Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ, with similar wording. Muslim, Aḥmad and the authors of the Sunan, except Abū Dāwūd, related it through several routes from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, whose name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mull. [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (2763); Musnad (1/385); Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (3114); al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā no. (11247); Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1398).]

Aḥmad, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Jarīr narrated, and this is his wording, through several routes from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, that he heard Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd narrate from ʿAlqamah and al-Aswad, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I found a woman in an orchard, and I did everything with her except that I did not have intercourse with her. I kissed her and embraced her, and I did nothing beyond that. So do to me whatever you will." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said nothing, and the man left. ʿUmar said: "Allah has concealed him; if only he had concealed himself." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent after him with his gaze, then said: "Bring him back to me." They brought him back, and he recited to him: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ Muʿādh said, and in the narration of ʿUmar: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for him alone, or for all people?" He said: "Rather, it is for all people." [Musnad (1/445); Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. (2763); Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (4468); Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (3112); al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā no. (7323); Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (15/515).]

Aḥmad said: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd related to us, Abān ibn Isḥāq related to us, from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Muḥammad, from Murrah al-Hamdānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has distributed your characters among you as He distributed your provisions among you. Allah gives the world to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, but He does not give the religion except to whomever He loves. So whoever Allah gives the religion has indeed loved him. By Him in whose hand is my soul, a servant does not submit until his heart and tongue submit, and he does not believe until his neighbour is safe from his evils." We said: "And what are his evils, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "His cheating and his oppression. A servant does not earn unlawful wealth and then spend from it, and be blessed in it, nor give charity from it and have it accepted, nor leave it behind his back except that it becomes his provision to the Fire. Indeed Allah does not erase an evil with an evil, but He erases an evil with a good. Indeed, the wicked does not erase the wicked." [Musnad (1/387).]

Ibn Jarīr said: Abū al-Sāʾib related to us, Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "So-and-so ibn Muʿattib was a man from the Anṣār, and he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I entered upon a woman and I did with her what a man does with his wife, except that I did not have intercourse with her.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not know how to answer him until this verse was revealed: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called him and recited it to him." [Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (15/519).]

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he was ʿAmr ibn Ghaziyyah al-Anṣārī, the date seller. Muqātil said: he was Abū Nufayl ʿĀmir ibn Qays al-Anṣārī. Al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī mentioned that he was Abū al-Yasar Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr.

Imām Aḥmad said: Yūnus and ʿAffān related to us, both saying: Ḥammād, that is Ibn Salamah, related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd. ʿAffān said: ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man came to ʿUmar and said: "A woman came to buy from me, so I brought her into the storeroom, and I touched her with what is less than intercourse." ʿUmar said: "Woe to you! Perhaps she was a woman whose husband is away in the way of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Go to Abū Bakr and ask him." He went to him and asked him, and he said: "Perhaps she is a woman whose husband is away in the way of Allah?" and he said the same as ʿUmar. Then he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to him the same thing, and he said: "Perhaps she is a woman whose husband is away in the way of Allah." Then the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ until the end of the verse. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for me alone, or for all people?" ʿUmar struck his chest with his hand and said: "No, and not even the coolness of the eye [i.e., no, not at all]; rather, it is for all people." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "ʿUmar has spoken the truth." [Musnad (1/245); ʿAlī ibn Zayd is weak.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 11, verses 114–115 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated through Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Uthman ibn Mawhib, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu al-Yasar Ka'b ibn 'Amr al-Ansari, who said: A woman came to me to buy dates from me for a dirham. I said: "In the house there are dates better and finer than these." So she entered, and I reached out to her and kissed her. I came to Umar and asked him, and he said: "Fear Allah, conceal yourself, and do not tell anyone." But I could not bear it, so I came to Abu Bakr and asked him, and he said: "Fear Allah, conceal yourself, and do not tell anyone." He said: I could not bear it, so I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him. He said: "Did you betray a man who is fighting in the way of Allah, regarding his family, with the like of this?" until I thought I was among the people of the Fire, and I wished that I had not embraced Islam at that hour. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lowered his head for a while, and Jibril descended and said: "Where is Abu al-Yasar?" I came, and he recited to me: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ up to ﴿a reminder for those who remember﴾. A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for him specifically, or for people in general?" He said: "For people in general" (Tafsir al-Tabari, 15/523).

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni said: Al-Husayn ibn Isma'il al-Mahamili narrated to us, Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that he was sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who had relations with a woman who was not lawful to him, and he did everything a man may do with his wife except intercourse?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Perform ablution well, then stand and pray." Mu'adh said: So Allah revealed this verse, meaning His saying: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night﴾. Mu'adh asked: "Is it for him specifically, or for the Muslims in general?" He said: "Rather, for the Muslims in general."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through several chains, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, with the same wording (Sunan al-Daraqutni, 1/134; Tafsir al-Tabari, 15/520–522). Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan, no. 3113, through Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr with the same wording, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This hadith does not have a connected isnad (chain). Abd Allah ibn Abi Layla did not hear from Mu'adh. Shu'bah narrated this hadith from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a mursal (a report where a Successor omits the Companion)."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah, that a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned a woman while he was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He asked his permission for a need, and he was permitted. He went to look for her but did not find her. The man then set out wanting to give the Prophet (ﷺ) the good news of rain, and he found the woman sitting by a pool. He pushed her in the chest and sat between her legs, and his member became like a tuft of hair (hudbah). He stood up regretful until he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what he had done. He said to him: "Ask forgiveness from your Lord, and pray four rak'ahs." He said: And he recited to him: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night﴾ to the end of the verse (Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq, 1/274).

Ibn Jarir said: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabwayh narrated to me, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me, Abd Allah ibn Salim narrated to me, from al-Zubaydi, from Salim ibn Amir, that he heard Abu Umamah say: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, enforce the legal punishment of Allah upon me" (he said it once or twice). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away from him. Then the prayer was called, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) finished the prayer, he said: "Where is this man who said: 'Enforce upon me the legal punishment of Allah?'" He said: "Here I am." He said: "Did you complete the ablution and pray with us just now?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you are free from your sin as on the day your mother bore you. Do not return to it." And Allah revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ (Tafsir al-Tabari, 15/521). Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, no. 2765, through Shaddad ibn Abd Allah, from Abu Umamah, with similar wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Abu Uthman, who said: I was with Salman al-Farisi under a tree. He took a dry branch from it and shook it until a leaf fell off. Then he said: "O Abu Uthman, will you not ask me why I do this?" I said: "Why do you do it?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did this to me when I was with him under a tree. He took a dry branch from it and shook it until a leaf fell off, and he said: 'O Salman, will you not ask me why I do this?'" I said: "And why do you do it?" He said: "When a Muslim performs ablution and does it well, then prays the five prayers, his sins fall away just as this leaf falls." And he said: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ (Musnad Ahmad, 5/437).

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O Mu'adh, follow the evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and treat people with good character" (Musnad Ahmad, 5/228).

Imam Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Maymun ibn Abi Shabib, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fear Allah wherever you are, follow the evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and treat people with good character" (Musnad Ahmad, 5/153).

Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shamr ibn 'Atiyyah, from his shaykhs, from Abu Dharr, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "When you commit an evil deed, follow it with a good deed and it will erase it." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is 'There is no god but Allah' among the good deeds?" He said: "It is the best of good deeds" (Musnad Ahmad, 5/169).

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Hudhayl ibn Ibrahim al-Jummani narrated to us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri narrated to us, from the descendants of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from al-Zuhri, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No servant says: 'There is no god but Allah' at any hour of night or day, except that the sins written in his record are wiped away, until he is at ease with the like of them in good deeds" (Musnad Abi Ya'la, 6/204). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/82): "In its chain is Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri, who is abandoned (matruk)."

Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman is called al-Waqqasi. There is weakness in him.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Bishr ibn Adam and Zayd ibn Akhram both narrated to us, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Mastur ibn Abbad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have left behind no need or small need (without addressing it)." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then this will cover that" (Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3067, Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/83): "Its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)").

Only Mastur narrated this hadith through this route.

Allah, exalted is He, says: "Why were there not, among the generations before you, remnants of people of goodness who would forbid the corruption and evil deeds that were taking place among them and the wrongdoing on the earth?"

* *

As for His saying, ﴿except a few﴾, meaning: there were indeed a few of such people among them, few in number. These are the ones whom Allah saved when His punishment descended and His retribution came suddenly. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, commanded this noble Ummah that there should be among it those who enjoin what is good (al-ma'ruf) and forbid what is evil (al-munkar), as He said: ﴿Let there be among you a community who call to goodness, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And those are the successful.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 104]. And in the hadith: "When people see the evil and do not change it, Allah is about to encompass them all with punishment." For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then why were there not, among the generations before you, people of virtue who forbade corruption on the earth, except a few of those whom We saved from among them?﴾

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And those who did wrong pursued the luxury they had been given therein﴾, meaning: they persisted in what they were engaged in of sins and evil deeds, and paid no attention to the denunciation of those people, until the punishment seized them suddenly. ﴿And they were criminals.﴾

Then Allah informed that He never destroys a town while its people are wrongdoers [to themselves] [[addition from manuscripts T and A]], and He never sends His might and punishment upon a town whose people are reformers, until they are the wrongdoers, as He said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ [Hud: 101], and He said: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat: 46].

Allah, exalted is He, says: "Why were there not, among the generations before you, remnants of people of goodness who would forbid the corruption and evil deeds that were taking place among them and the wrongdoing on the earth?"

* *

As for His saying, ﴿except a few﴾, meaning: there were indeed a few of such people among them, few in number. These are the ones whom Allah saved when His punishment descended and His retribution came suddenly. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, commanded this noble Ummah that there should be among it those who enjoin what is good (al-ma'ruf) and forbid what is evil (al-munkar), as He said: ﴿Let there be among you a community who call to goodness, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And those are the successful.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 104]. And in the hadith: "When people see the evil and do not change it, Allah is about to encompass them all with punishment." For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then why were there not, among the generations before you, people of virtue who forbade corruption on the earth, except a few of those whom We saved from among them?﴾

* *

Then Allah informed that He never destroys a town while its people are wrongdoers [to themselves] [[addition from manuscripts T and A]], and He never sends His might and punishment upon a town whose people are reformers, until they are the wrongdoers, as He said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ [Hud: 101], and He said: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat: 46].

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 11, verses 118–119:

He, may He be exalted, informs that He is able to make all people one community (ummah), whether in faith or in disbelief, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, everyone on earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ [Yunus: 99].

* *

His saying: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾ means: the disagreement among people concerning their religions, their beliefs, their creeds (milal), their sects (nihal), their schools of thought (madhahib) and their opinions will not cease.

'Ikrimah said: "﴿Differing﴾ concerning guidance." [In T and A: "concerning desire (al-hawa)."]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "﴿Differing﴾ concerning provision, so some of them subjugate others." The well-known and sound view is the first.

* *

His saying: ﴿except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾ means: except those who are shown mercy among the followers of the messengers, who held fast to what they were commanded of the religion [In T: "the religion which"; in A: "the religion, those who"]. The messengers of Allah informed them of it, and this remained their custom, until the Prophet (ﷺ), the unlettered one, the seal of the messengers and prophets, came. They followed him, believed him, supported him and aided him, and so they attained the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, because they are the saved group (al-firqah al-najiyah). This is as came in the hadith narrated in the Musnads and the Sunan, through chains that strengthen one another: "The Jews split into seventy-one sects, the Christians split into seventy-two sects, and my community will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect." They said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Those who are upon what I am upon and my companions." [In A: "two sects" for the Jews, and "this community" for "my community".]

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak with this addition. [Its takhrij was previously mentioned at the explanation of verse 93 of Surah Yunus.]

'Ata' said: ﴿And they will not cease to differ﴾ refers to the Jews, the Christians and the Magians; ﴿except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾ refers to the Hanifiyyah (the pure monotheistic faith).

Qatadah said: "The people of Allah's mercy are the people of the Jama'ah (the main body of the community), even if their dwellings and bodies are scattered, and the people of His disobedience are the people of division, even if their dwellings and bodies are gathered."

* *

His saying: ﴿And for that He created them﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri, in one narration from him, said: "And for the disagreement He created them."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "He created them as two groups," like His saying: ﴿So among them is the wretched and the happy﴾ [Hud: 105].

It was also said: "He created them for mercy." Ibn Wahb said: Muslim ibn Khalid informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Tawus, that two men brought a dispute before him and argued at length. Tawus said: "You differed and you argued excessively!" One of the two men said: "For that we were created." Tawus said: "You lie." He said: "Does not Allah say: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy, and for that He created them﴾?" Tawus said: "He did not create them so that they would differ, but He created them for the Jama'ah and for mercy."

Likewise, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He created them for mercy, and He did not create them for punishment." Likewise said Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Qatadah. The meaning of this view returns to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56].

It was also said: rather, the intended meaning is: "He created them for mercy and for disagreement." This is as al-Hasan al-Basri said in one narration from him regarding His saying: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy, and for that He created them﴾. He said: "People differ over diverse religions, but those upon whom your Lord has mercy do not differ." It was said to him: "So for that He created them?" He said: "He created these for His Paradise, He created these for His Fire, He created these for His mercy, and He created these for His punishment."

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and al-A'mash said likewise.

Ibn Wahb said: I asked Malik about His saying: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy, and for that He created them﴾. He said: "A group will be in Paradise and a group in the Blaze."

Ibn Jarir chose this view, as did Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Farra'.

From Malik, in what we have related from him in the Tafsir: ﴿And for that He created them﴾, he said: "For mercy." Others said: "For disagreement."

* *

His saying: ﴿But the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men, all together"﴾ informs that He, may He be exalted, had already decreed in His predestination and divine decree, with His perfect knowledge and His far-reaching wisdom, that among those He created are those who deserve Paradise and among them are those who deserve the Fire, and that He will surely fill Hell with these two weighty things, the jinn and mankind. He has the conclusive proof and perfect wisdom.

In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. Paradise said: 'What is the matter with me that only the weak among people and their lowly enter me?' The Fire said: 'I have been given the arrogant and the tyrannical.' Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are My punishment; I inflict punishment through you on whomever I will, and each of you will have its fill.' As for Paradise, there will still be room in it, until Allah creates for it a creation to fill the room of Paradise. As for the Fire, it will keep saying: 'Is there more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot upon it, and it says: 'Enough, enough, by Your might!'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7449, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2846.]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 11, verses 118–119:

He, may He be exalted, informs that He is able to make all people one community (ummah), whether in faith or in disbelief, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, everyone on earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ [Yunus: 99].

* *

His saying: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾ means: the disagreement among people concerning their religions, their beliefs, their creeds (milal), their sects (nihal), their schools of thought (madhahib) and their opinions will not cease.

'Ikrimah said: "﴿Differing﴾ concerning guidance." [In T and A: "concerning desire (al-hawa)."]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "﴿Differing﴾ concerning provision, so some of them subjugate others." The well-known and sound view is the first.

* *

His saying: ﴿except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾ means: except those who are shown mercy among the followers of the messengers, who held fast to what they were commanded of the religion [In T: "the religion which"; in A: "the religion, those who"]. The messengers of Allah informed them of it, and this remained their custom, until the Prophet (ﷺ), the unlettered one, the seal of the messengers and prophets, came. They followed him, believed him, supported him and aided him, and so they attained the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, because they are the saved group (al-firqah al-najiyah). This is as came in the hadith narrated in the Musnads and the Sunan, through chains that strengthen one another: "The Jews split into seventy-one sects, the Christians split into seventy-two sects, and my community will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect." They said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Those who are upon what I am upon and my companions." [In A: "two sects" for the Jews, and "this community" for "my community".]

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak with this addition. [Its takhrij was previously mentioned at the explanation of verse 93 of Surah Yunus.]

'Ata' said: ﴿And they will not cease to differ﴾ refers to the Jews, the Christians and the Magians; ﴿except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾ refers to the Hanifiyyah (the pure monotheistic faith).

Qatadah said: "The people of Allah's mercy are the people of the Jama'ah (the main body of the community), even if their dwellings and bodies are scattered, and the people of His disobedience are the people of division, even if their dwellings and bodies are gathered."

* *

His saying: ﴿And for that He created them﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri, in one narration from him, said: "And for the disagreement He created them."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "He created them as two groups," like His saying: ﴿So among them is the wretched and the happy﴾ [Hud: 105].

It was also said: "He created them for mercy." Ibn Wahb said: Muslim ibn Khalid informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Tawus, that two men brought a dispute before him and argued at length. Tawus said: "You differed and you argued excessively!" One of the two men said: "For that we were created." Tawus said: "You lie." He said: "Does not Allah say: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy, and for that He created them﴾?" Tawus said: "He did not create them so that they would differ, but He created them for the Jama'ah and for mercy."

Likewise, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He created them for mercy, and He did not create them for punishment." Likewise said Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Qatadah. The meaning of this view returns to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56].

It was also said: rather, the intended meaning is: "He created them for mercy and for disagreement." This is as al-Hasan al-Basri said in one narration from him regarding His saying: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy, and for that He created them﴾. He said: "People differ over diverse religions, but those upon whom your Lord has mercy do not differ." It was said to him: "So for that He created them?" He said: "He created these for His Paradise, He created these for His Fire, He created these for His mercy, and He created these for His punishment."

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and al-A'mash said likewise.

Ibn Wahb said: I asked Malik about His saying: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy, and for that He created them﴾. He said: "A group will be in Paradise and a group in the Blaze."

Ibn Jarir chose this view, as did Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Farra'.

From Malik, in what we have related from him in the Tafsir: ﴿And for that He created them﴾, he said: "For mercy." Others said: "For disagreement."

* *

His saying: ﴿But the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men, all together"﴾ informs that He, may He be exalted, had already decreed in His predestination and divine decree, with His perfect knowledge and His far-reaching wisdom, that among those He created are those who deserve Paradise and among them are those who deserve the Fire, and that He will surely fill Hell with these two weighty things, the jinn and mankind. He has the conclusive proof and perfect wisdom.

In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. Paradise said: 'What is the matter with me that only the weak among people and their lowly enter me?' The Fire said: 'I have been given the arrogant and the tyrannical.' Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are My punishment; I inflict punishment through you on whomever I will, and each of you will have its fill.' As for Paradise, there will still be room in it, until Allah creates for it a creation to fill the room of Paradise. As for the Fire, it will keep saying: 'Is there more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot upon it, and it says: 'Enough, enough, by Your might!'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7449, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2846.]

Allah the Exalted says: And all the accounts that We relate to you, of the messengers who came before you along with their peoples, and how their disputes and contentions with their peoples went, and what the prophets endured of denial and harm, and how Allah gave victory to His party of believers and humiliated His enemies, the disbelievers, all of this is what We use to strengthen your heart, O Muhammad, that is, your heart, so that you may have in those messengers who passed before you, your brothers, an example.

* *

His saying, ﴿And there has come to you in this the truth﴾, means: in [this] [[Addition from A.]] this sūrah (chapter). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and a group of the salaf (the early generations). And it is reported from al-Hasan, in one narration from him, and Qatadah: in this world.

The correct view is: in this sūrah, which includes the stories of the prophets and how Allah saved them and the believers with them, and destroyed the disbelievers. There has come to you in it a true account, a genuine report, an admonition by which the disbelievers are restrained, and a reminder by which the believers are made to take heed. [[In T, A: "anjahum" (he saved them).]] [[In T, A: "yatadhakkar" (is mindful).]]

Almighty Allah says, commanding His Messenger to say to those who do not believe in what he has brought from his Lord, by way of threat: ﴿Act according to your position﴾, i.e., according to your way and your method. ﴿Indeed, we are acting﴾, i.e., according to our way and our method. ﴿And wait; indeed, we are waiting﴾, i.e., you will soon know who will have the good end of the abode. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾

Allah has indeed fulfilled His promise to His Messenger, and He granted him victory and support, and made His word the highest, and the word of those who disbelieved the lowest. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

Almighty Allah says, commanding His Messenger to say to those who do not believe in what he has brought from his Lord, by way of threat: ﴿Act according to your position﴾, i.e., according to your way and your method. ﴿Indeed, we are acting﴾, i.e., according to our way and our method. ﴿And wait; indeed, we are waiting﴾, i.e., you will soon know who will have the good end of the abode. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾

Allah has indeed fulfilled His promise to His Messenger, and He granted him victory and support, and made His word the highest, and the word of those who disbelieved the lowest. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

Ibn Kathir says: God, exalted is He, informs that He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and that to Him is the return and the final resort, and that He will fully recompense every doer for his deed on the Day of Reckoning. To Him belong creation and command. Therefore He commanded that He alone be worshipped and relied upon, for He is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him and turns to Him in repentance.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾ [[In manuscript T: "ya'malun" (they do).]], meaning: nothing is hidden from Him of what your deniers, O Muhammad, are engaged in. Rather, He is Knowing of their circumstances and their words, and He will recompense them for that with the most complete recompense in this world and the Hereafter, and He will grant you and your party victory over them in both abodes. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn WakI' related to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab related to us, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from Abdullah ibn Rabah, from Ka'b [[In manuscript A: "Ka'b al-Ahbar".]] who said: "The conclusion of the Torah is the conclusion of Hud" [and Allah knows best]. [[Addition from manuscript A.]] The commentary on Surah Hud is complete.
